news.Title: Is Alphabet's Massive AI Spending a Problem? The CFO Just Revealed Everything Investors Need to Know in a Single Sentence.
news.Content:
Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL) is spending more cash than it's generating, and investors are worried. The company's capital expenditures totaled $51.4 billion last quarter, mostly related to its artificial intelligence (AI) compute build-out. That number could continue to climb in the fourth quarter and in 2027.

Many investors are concerned that Alphabet is overextending itself, raising additional capital to fund a speculative investment. That sentiment caused shares to tumble after the company's third-quarter earnings release. For long-term investors, the most important detail came during the company's earnings call, when CFO Anat Ashkenazi revealed everything you need to know in a single sentence.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The investment thesis for Alphabet has changed

For years, Alphabet ran a business with extremely low capital intensity. It collected ad revenue from web searches (Google) and user-generated videos (YouTube). Its dominance in both categories made it a highly profitable business, and it used some of those profits to invest in moonshots (Other Bets) and buy back its stock. Investors could count on strong free cash flow generation quarter after quarter, but Alphabet's opportunities to deploy its excess cash were relatively limited.

With the AI boom, Alphabet has found the opportunity to deploy that cash. In fact, it has an opportunity to deploy more cash than it has, hence why it's raised tens of billions in equity and debt over the last few years. It raised $40 billion last quarter alone.

CFO Anat Ashkenazi explained exactly why the company is raising additional capital to fund the build-out. "Throughout this investment cycle, we expect to generate an attractive ROIC that remains meaningfully above our cost of capital and anticipate generating strong cash flow from operations," she said during the third-quarter earnings call.

Warren Buffett agrees. He initiated a position in Alphabet stock for Berkshire Hathaway last year, which has now grown to be the conglomerate's fourth-largest position in its marketable equity portfolio. His thesis was that Alphabet has an opportunity to generate a high return on capital while putting an enormous amount of capital to work.

Not only is Alphabet positioned to invest a ton of capital, but its massive spending also might not have nearly as much risk as the market is pricing in.

Story Continues

Alphabet's massive advantage

Alphabet has an advantage over other hyperscalers for generating a strong return on invested capital: It's the only company with a full stack of artificial intelligence products and services. It designs popular Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) chips for both training and inference. TPU chips are gaining broad adoption among leading developers, and Alphabet is now selling TPU systems directly to third parties.

Alphabet also develops its own frontier large language models. Use of those models runs on Google Cloud. It runs a security and governance platform for AI. And it's an end user of AI itself, with integrations for its core Search product on both the search results and advertising sides, not to mention its Gemini chat app that now counts over 1 billion users.

That level of vertical integration can lead to lower cost of ownership and shorter payback periods for its AI data center spending. That's supported by Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian's assertion that its server spending (about 65% of total capex last quarter) has a payback period of less than two years. For its own TPU systems, the payback period is half of that.

That payback period compares very favorably with other disclosures from competing hyperscalers. Amazon , for example, said its payback period for its servers and networking equipment is nearly three years.

The long-term payoff for Alphabet could be massive. Free cash flow could rise from around $50 billion (adjusted for stock-based compensation) before the investment cycle to more than $300 billion by 2031, according to the average forecast from analysts. That speaks to the high potential return on invested capital for Alphabet's cloud infrastructure.

That said, investors should expect a deeper drop in free cash flow in 2027 as spending continues to ramp up. Keep in mind Ashkenazi's statement that ROIC remains meaningfully above the cost of capital. As long as that remains true, the value of the business improves with each dollar invested in new data centers.

news.Title: Tesla-SpaceX merger math just shifted in Tesla's favor
news.Content: When two companies merge with stock, nobody hands you cash. You trade one set of shares for another and hope the swap was fair. That trade happens whether you pay attention or not. If you own a broad index fund, it can happen inside your 401(k) without a single click from you. Tesla (TSLA) is big enough that plenty of people hold it that way. The automaker reported $28.05 billion in third-quarter revenue and delivered 486,532 vehicles. SpaceX (SPCX) is worth about $1.83 trillion, and Tesla about $1.58 trillion. Elon Musk runs both, and he sees "a lot of merit" in combining them, he said on SpaceX's Oct. 20 earnings call. However, a subtle shift has emerged in how Wall Street talks about a deal. The question is no longer whether it makes sense. It's what Tesla shareholders would actually get. According to a Bank of America research report seen by TheStreet, Tesla holders should expect a premium if SpaceX buys the company, but a tough shareholder vote and China stand in the way. What a Tesla-SpaceX swap would look like by the numbers Terms haven't been agreed upon, and a deal is far from certain. Musk himself called the Tesla vote "quite a high hurdle." Analyst Alexander Perry laid out the math in an Oct. 29 note titled "Thrusters included: Potential merger adds optionality on top of the autonomy ramp." "We think a logical structure could be an all-stock acquisition of Tesla by SpaceX, with Tesla shareholders receiving newly issued SpaceX shares," wrote Perry. Related: Elon Musk doubles down on the Roadster with SpaceX thrusters At Oct. 20 closing values, a swap with no premium would leave Tesla holders with 42.4% of the combined company, Perry wrote. Musk would hold 36.3% of the economics and 55.6% of the vote. Perry expects the Tesla board's special committee to push for more. Here's how his scenarios stack up: No premium: About $374 a Tesla share, with Tesla holders owning 42.4% 20% premium: About $449 a share, with Tesla holders owning 46.9% 25% premium: About $467 a share, with Tesla holders owning 47.9% 30% premium: About $486 a share, with Tesla holders owning 48.9% Even at a 30% premium, Musk would keep 51.6% of the vote, the note showed. Why the market already moved the math Here's the part I'd focus on. The stocks have moved since Oct. 20, and that changes the starting point. More on Tesla and SpaceX: SpaceX shares soar on possible tie-up with Tesla Bank of America sends SpaceX stock investors strong signal Tesla stock sellers should pump their brakes, 5-star analyst says Story Continues Tesla closed at $399.81 on Oct. 30. SpaceX fell 6.4% that day to $134.72. By my math, an at-market swap at those prices works out to about 2.97 SpaceX shares per Tesla share. That's close to the 3.03 ratio in Perry's 20% premium case. Using the share counts in his note, Tesla holders would own about 46% of the combined company with no premium at all. In other words, the market has already handed Tesla holders part of the premium Perry expects them to negotiate. That cuts both ways. A committee asking for 25% on top of today's price would be asking SpaceX for a lot more stock. Given that backdrop, it's easy to understand why Perry thinks the strategic case rests on shared costs rather than goodwill. The clearest example is Terafab, the companies' joint chip project. The companies "have yet to agree how to split Terafab's costs, which Musk expects to exceed $100bn long term, and a merger would remove that negotiation," wrote Perry. The business ties already run deep. SpaceX bought $626 million of Tesla Megapacks through the third quarter, including $221 million in the third quarter alone, Perry wrote. The vote and China could still stop it Bank of America sees two big hurdles before any premium matters. The first is the vote. Tesla's charter requires approval from a majority of all outstanding shares, and abstentions and broker non-votes count against a deal, Perry wrote. He pointed to 2025 as a warning. Tesla's advisory proposal to invest in xAI drew 1.06 billion votes for and 916 million against, but it still failed on 473 million abstentions, the note showed. By my math, abstentions made up about 19% of the votes cast on that proposal. A merger vote would face an even higher bar, because unvoted shares would also count as no votes. The second hurdle is China. "We view China as the main regulatory risk as a potential deal would place Tesla's Shanghai plant, which builds roughly half of its global vehicle output, under a major U.S. defense contractor," wrote Perry. He expects a firewall that keeps Tesla China's data and staff apart from SpaceX's defense work, the approach used by companies such as Airbus and Honeywell. Much will likely depend, however, on timing. Bloomberg reported a push to announce a deal by the first half of 2027, Perry noted, though the companies haven't confirmed it. Tesla's Dec. 3 annual meeting doesn't include a merger vote. I'd also keep an eye on the money. Perry forecasts negative free cash flow of $4.6 billion this year and $11.3 billion in 2027 as capital spending climbs to about $25 billion a year, the note showed. A cash-hungry Tesla gives SpaceX the upper hand at the bargaining table. Perry kept his Buy rating and $460 price objective, about 15% above Tesla's Oct. 30 close, by my math. "We see a potential merger as additive optionality on top," wrote Perry. Related: Bank of America resets Tesla forecast as Robotaxi miles double This story was originally published by TheStreet on Nov 2, 2026, where it first appeared in the Markets section. news.Title: 外資賣超破2.3兆！上週狂砍1733億 「這檔」被倒貨10萬張最慘
news.Content:

外資上週賣超與累計動向

news.Title: Asia stocks rise as tech gains ahead of Apple results
news.Content:
Investing.com-- Most Asian stocks rose on Monday, with technology shares leading gains as easing oil prices supported risk appetite, while investors awaited quarterly results from Apple amid concerns over heavy artificial intelligence spending.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

U.S. stock futures also advanced in Asian trading by 04:03 GMT, offering some relief after Wall Street's sharp selloff last week.

Tech stocks rise ahead of Apple results

South Korea's KOSPI jumped 2.6%, with SK Hynix (KS:000660) climbing 4% and Samsung Electronics (KS:005930) rising 1.5%.

Japan's Nikkei 225 pared early losses to trade 0.4% higher, while the broader TOPIX index slipped 0.4%.

Investors were awaiting Apple's (NASDAQ:AAPL) earnings later on Monday, with the company's performance and outlook expected to offer an indication of whether consumer demand can help offset mounting concerns over the enormous costs of AI infrastructure investment.

Investors will also look for commentary on early demand for its iPhone 18 range, with pre-orders having started in mid-October.

Technology stocks remained in focus after Intel plunged nearly 29% on Friday following a disappointing profit outlook, raising concerns about the earnings prospects of semiconductor companies and other AI-related businesses.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Elsewhere in Asia, China's blue-chip Shanghai Shenzhen CSI 300 index climbed 1.3%, while the Shanghai Composite index rose 1.2%.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng gained 0.6%, with the Hang Seng TECH sub-index climbing 3%.

Oil prices ease; RBA decision awaited

Oil prices eased, providing some support to equity markets, as diplomatic efforts continued to end the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. Brent crude futures fell 2% to $111.15 a barrel, while U.S. crude declined 2.3% to $101.73.

India's Nifty 50 index rose 1.1%.

Bucking the trend, Australia's S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.5%, while Singapore's Straits Times Index dropped 1.4%.

Investors were also positioning for the Reserve Bank of Australia's policy decision on Tuesday. The central bank is widely expected to raise its cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85%, which would be its fifth increase this year, after lifting the rate to 4.60% in September.

The rate outlook has hardened after data showed Australian consumer price inflation accelerated to 4.3% in September from 4.0% in August.

Story Continues

RBA Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser has warned that the inflation outlook looks materially worse than previously projected, while Governor Michele Bullock said some upside risks had materialised.

news.Title: Stocks bounce as Apple earnings near, oil falls
news.Content:
By Wayne Cole

SYDNEY, Nov 2 (Reuters) - Share markets bounced in Asia on Monday as investors hoped for Apple earnings later in the session to provide some relief from AI cash-burn worries, while oil prices slid after talks continued between Iranian and Qatari mediators.

Brent futures fell 3.3% to $109.70 a barrel, ‌though that follows a 13.6% jump in October and tankers were still being attacked in the Gulf. US crude futures lost 3.4% to $100.58 a barrel. [O/R]

Apple has ‌been an oasis of relative calm given it does not spend billions on data centres, and its shares have climbed for four months straight to help it unseat Nvidia as the world's most valuable listed company.

Analysts ​are looking for quarterly earnings per share (EPS) of $2 on revenue of $113 billion, up from $1.85 in the year-earlier period. The company might also offer some guidance on how early sales of the iPhone 18 are performing with pre-orders having started in mid-October.

The optimism helped S&P 500 futures edge up 0.5%, while Nasdaq futures rallied 0.9%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq lost almost 7% in October for its worst month since the 'Liberation Day' tariff rout of April 2025.

Some upbeat news is sorely needed after concerns about negative cash flow and the sheer scale of AI capex saw ‌the cost of insuring against corporate defaults blow out last ⁠week.

Intel's near 29% tumble on Friday has also raised the stakes for other chip groups, including AMD.

An added wrinkle is the midterm US elections, where a win by Democrats in either or both houses could result in more political hurdles for data centres.

Analysts at Goldman Sachs ⁠expect capex by hyperscalers to almost double to $800 billion this year, and rise further to $1.2 trillion in 2027. At the same time, they see the S&P 500 EPS growth of nearly 30% in 2026 slowing to 18% next year.

"Earnings results have underscored the fundamental challenge facing equity investors — earnings growth is strong, but it is no longer accelerating," wrote Ben Snider, Goldman's chief US equity ​strategist, ​in a note.

"Similarly, Q3 results support our view that AI investment spending will continue to grow ​but that the growth rate of AI capex is peaking."

Adding to ‌the air of unease were withdrawals from Binance as the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange went back online on Sunday after hackers stole billions from the platform last week.

Japan's Nikkei firmed 0.3%, while South Korea added 2.6%, having shed 16% last month. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.5%.

Story Continues

China's battered blue chips gained 1.3% after media reports said regulators would meet financial institutions to discuss measures to support capital markets.

In Europe, EUROSTOXX 50 futures rose 0.3%, while DAX futures firmed 0.2% and FTSE futures were flat.

MORE RATE HIKES COMING

The retreat in equities last month provided a reprieve to safe-haven bonds, with investors wondering if a sustained selloff in the stock market could deter the Federal Reserve from hiking ‌interest rates in December.

Futures still imply a 72% chance of a quarter-point rate rise, but now ​only have 55 basis points of total tightening priced in compared to more than 70 basis points a ​month ago.

Yields on 10-year Treasuries held at 4.931%, well off their October peak ​of 5.3645%, while 2-year yields stood at 4.612%. Treasury will announce its quarterly refunding plans on Wednesday, which could see more issuance at ‌the shorter end of the curve.

Among central banks meeting this week, ​markets are wagering on hikes from the Reserve ​Bank of Australia, Bank of England and Riksbank, while the Norges Bank is seen on hold.

Economic data due this week includes the influential US ISM survey of manufacturing for October later on Monday, while the all-important payrolls report is on Friday.

Median forecasts are for a 65,000 rise in jobs, after September's disappointing 29,000 gain, ​with the unemployment rate holding at 4.2%.

In currency markets, the ‌majors were pretty much sidelined while all the action was concentrated in stocks. The euro was a shade firmer at $1.1169, while the dollar was barely ​changed at 157.75 yen.

Non-interest-bearing gold bounced 0.9% to $3,911 an ounce, having fallen 6.8% last month amid talk some investors were having to sell to ​cover margin calls on equities. [GOL/]

(Reporting by Wayne Cole; Editing by Shri Navaratnam and Muralikumar Anantharaman)

news.Title: 櫃買指數逆勢翻紅漲近1%！分析師點名環球晶當「多頭司令」
news.Content:
台股今（2）日一度挫逾800點，但櫃買指數卻率先由黑翻紅，盤中上漲近1%，表現相對強勢。啟發投顧分析師丁彥鈞表示，櫃買指數主要是技術面跌深反彈，KD指標已降至20附近，但不代表長線跌勢結束，後續仍可能有約1成修正空間。若上櫃股展開反彈，他看好群聯（8299）、環球晶（6488），其中又以環球晶有望成為上櫃股反彈的「多頭司令」。

觀察今日盤勢，櫃買指數早盤最低下探362.18點，隨後買盤回流，由黑翻紅，盤中最高來到373.22點。相較加權指數，中小型股表現相對強勢。

丁彥鈞指出，櫃買指數近期已跌破半年線，技術面明顯轉弱，但隨著KD指標降至20附近，短線出現跌深反彈。他強調，今天盤中翻紅主要是技術性反彈。

丁彥鈞表示，櫃買指數目前本益比約25.77倍，仍處於相對偏高水準，若未來美國升息、外資持續賣超，本益比可能向20倍靠攏，但不代表指數還會再下跌2成，因為企業的獲利有成長，預估櫃買指數可能再下跌1成左右。

至於哪些上櫃股有機會率先帶動反彈，丁彥鈞點名群聯及環球晶，認為兩家公司基本面較佳，有望成為後續反彈的觀察指標。若只能選出一檔作為「多頭司令」，他則看好環球晶，主要是環球晶位於半導體產業上游，對景氣變化的反應較為敏感。

丁彥鈞也預估，櫃買指數350點附近有機會形成支撐，跌破的機率不高。不過，他提醒，短線跌深反彈與長線趨勢反轉仍有差別，投資人不宜僅因指數盤中翻紅，就認定修正行情已經結束。

news.Title: Intel Shares Collapse. Why I'm Still Not Buying the Stock
news.Content:
Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) shares collapsed after the chipmaker issued weak Q4 guidance amid a slowdown in the PC market. Before its earnings report, the stock had been on a huge run, up about 150% year-to-date, benefiting from the rise of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) and the sudden surge in demand for server central processing units (CPUs).

However, even with the stock getting crushed, I still wouldn't buy it. The semiconductor stock got way too far ahead of itself for a company that has been losing market share in the data center CPU market and losing money in its struggling foundry business. At the same time, the stock went from cheap relative to its physical assets (tangible book value) to one that looked overvalued.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Let's take a closer look at Intel's Q3 report and prospects and why I still don't think the stock is a buy even after this pullback.

PC slowdown hits the stock

Intel's Q3 results were quite solid, with revenue up 21% to $16.5 billion. However, that was a deceleration from Q2's 25% growth and was just in line with analyst estimates, as compiled by LSEG .

Intel's biggest growth driver was once again server CPUs, with the company seeing its strongest data center growth in 15 years. With the rise of AI agents, server CPUs have been in high demand, while supply has been tight. In fact, Intel called it one of the largest supply shortages the industry has seen

This led to Intel's data center and AI (DCAI) revenue surging 78% to $7.3 billion in the quarter. Meanwhile, DCAI operating income more than tripled from $964 million to $3 billion.

The growth was led by newer-generation CPUs, with the company saying that since Q1, its 18A client CPUs have gone from less than 5% of revenue to nearly a third. Meanwhile, 18A costs have fallen by 40% as it's seen continued improvements in yield and cycle time.

Intel expects the strong demand for server CPUs to continue. It sees server CPU industry unit growth of 30% in both this year and next, noting it would be higher in both years if not for supply constraints. Meanwhile, it sees CPU industry revenue climbing fivefold over the next five years from $40 billion to $200 billion.

While its data center segment was strong, Intel's larger client computing and physical AI group (CCPG) struggled, with Q3 revenue falling 5% to $8.1 billion. Segment operating income, meanwhile, declined by 15% to $2.3 billion.

Story Continues

The weakness stemmed from a struggling PC market, which has seen sales decline due to higher prices (driven by skyrocketing memory prices) and IT budget constraints. Intel thinks this weakness will continue through 2027, projecting a 10% decline in units following a 12% decrease this year. This will also come with an inventory correction that will hit it the hardest in Q4 and Q1.

Adding to Intel's woes, the company will see a $600 million revenue hit over the next two quarters due to an explosion at one of its fabs in Israel.

Intel's foundry business, meanwhile, saw revenue soar 58% to $6.7 billion. However, the segment continues to post large operating losses, with a $1.9 billion loss in the quarter. Revenue from Intel's other businesses dropped 30% year over year to $0.7 billion, largely due to its earlier sale of 51% of its Altera subsidiary.

Gross margins had been an issue for Intel, but they've nicely rebounded. Gross margin climbed 4,800 basis points to 43% in the quarter, while adjusted gross margin rose 4,100 basis points. This helped lead its adjusted EPS to surge 126% to $0.52, easily topping the $0.40 consensus.

Looking ahead, Intel projected Q4 revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion with adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $0.25. That was well below the $0.43 EPS and $17.1 billion in sales that analysts were expecting. It projected gross margins to be around 37%.

Avoid Intel stock

Intel is seeing strong momentum in the server CPU market, and it has a big opportunity ahead as this market grows rapidly. However, the company has been losing share in the space and is expected to continue losing it to Advanced Micro Devices , ARM Holdings , and ARM-based custom CPUs.

At the same time, the company is facing heavy pressure in the PC space, which is still its largest business, and the next two quarters are likely to be rough due to inventory adjustments. And while its foundry business has also seen revenue growth pick up, the segment is still seeing significant losses.

While the stock has fallen to a more reasonable forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 30 times based on 2027 analyst estimates, I do not think Intel deserves to trade at a premium multiple given the headwinds it is facing. I'd continue to avoid Intel's stock , as there are more attractive AI stocks out there to buy.

news.Title: Stock futures jump ahead of a monster week after a $5 trillion AI rout
news.Content:
Stock futures opened higher Sunday evening as Wall Street prepares for a week packed with Apple earnings, the midterm elections and $100 oil.

S&P 500 futures ( ES=F ), Nasdaq 100 futures ( NQ=F ) and Dow futures ( YM=F ) were all higher, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq leading the way after last week's AI selloff.

The selloff that closed out October was brutal but narrow. The biggest AI and chip stocks have lost about $5 trillion in market value since Oct. 6, by Yahoo Finance calculations, while the other 625 large US stocks in that tally added about $1.3 trillion.

Last week drove it home. The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) slipped about 0.6%, yet 9 of its 11 sectors rose about 1% or more. No other down week for the index since at least 1999 has had more than seven, by Yahoo Finance calculations.

What comes next is up for debate. One read of history says the tech meltdown could get a lot worse before it's over. Another says the stock market's sweetest stretch starts now : from the end of a midterm October through the following June, the S&P 500 has risen every time since 1950. Both could turn out to be true, since the October selloff showed the rest of the market can climb while tech sinks.

What's next

Apple. Apple ( AAPL ) reports after the bell Monday , with iPhone 18 sales in the spotlight, as the world's most valuable company again. It closed Friday worth about $5.03 trillion, ahead of Nvidia ( NVDA ) at about $4.93 trillion, and it's the only "Magnificent Seven" stock beating the S&P 500 this year, up about 27% vs. about 11%. Palantir ( PLTR ) also reports Monday.

Oil. West Texas Intermediate crude ( CL=F ) opened lower Sunday after settling Friday above $104 a barrel, its highest close since mid-September. The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively shut in the ninth month of the Iran war, and OPEC+ held its December output targets steady on Sunday .

The midterms and jobs. Voters go to the polls Tuesday, and the October jobs report comes Friday, with Wall Street debating whether the Fed put is back . Here's the full week ahead .

news.Title: 聯電、台達電操作方法曝光！南亞科、華邦電...6檔散戶避風港
news.Content:
受美國科技股與人工智慧族群持續修正，台股跌破半年線之後賣壓仍沉重，今（2日）早盤暴跌超過800點摔破45K，分析師提醒散戶投資人後市，並公開3大資金避風港，以及熱門股聯電與台達電的操作方式。

國泰證期顧問分析師郭經緯於Youtube頻道指出，市場下殺的壓力主要來自人工智慧交易的隱憂，以及科技巨頭財報的衝擊，現在市場更關心鉅額投資的回收速度，現金流與資本支出壓力，但人工智慧產業仍是長線成長的主軸，短線上的修正反而可以適時檢視基本面與投資價值。

賣壓重 聯電、台達電怎操作？

台股這一波修正中，台達電與聯電雙雙在法說會後重挫，引發散戶投資人恐慌。郭經緯表示，聯電第三季毛利率達34%，並追加32億美元的資本支出，成熟製程報價也將調漲10%，但漲價幅度不如市場預期，外資也出現調節。

操作建議上，郭經緯認為，聯電在年線100元附近可留意投資機會，基本面上具備支撐力道，且殖利率與特殊製程上也具有優勢。

至於台達電的狀況，郭經緯提到，短期營運出現干擾，但電源與液冷散熱依然是長線重要動能，待外資賣壓消化、股價量縮築底後，股價落在1200元以下可留意價值投資機會。

避風港？優先觀察3大族群6檔指標

台股資金避風港，郭經緯點名記憶體、IC設計及機電工具機等三大族群，主要是震盪期間的強勢股，指標包括周線上漲、產業獲利持續成長，且技術面已經過整理，從底部向上轉強、帶動均線翻揚，呼籲同時利用基本面與技術面篩選。

機電與工具機族群中，郭經緯提到上銀的短線壓力落在345元，新代的壓力落在2130元，只要能有效突破，就有機會挑戰5月前波高點；記憶體族群則關注南亞科與華邦電，本益比均不到5倍，南亞科留意493元季線壓力，華邦電則提防173元附近的壓力。

IC設計供應鏈中，郭經緯認為，矽力技術線型相對強勢，群聯壓力落在2035元附近，後續仍有機會挑戰前波高點，主要是兩檔個股經過波段修正後，投信已出現逢低布局跡象。

news.Title: Tesla, Samsung oppose new US tariffs on Vietnam as probe deadline nears
news.Content:
By Francesco Guarascio

HANOI, Nov 2 (Reuters) - Businesses are divided over whether Washington should propose new tariffs on Vietnamese goods this month, with Tesla and Samsung not in favour, while others have called for penalties, submissions to the ‌US government show.

The Trump administration has set a November 29 deadline to conclude a trade probe launched in May ‌over the Southeast Asian nation's alleged intellectual property violations. It designated Vietnam as a "priority foreign country", the first jurisdiction in 13 years to be added to the ​most serious US watchlist category.

The US has accused Vietnam of "a persistent failure to resolve long-standing concerns about IP protection and enforcement." A separate probe into alleged excessive capacity is also underway. Vietnam has urged Washington to conduct its investigations objectively.

It is not clear if any tariffs linked to IP violations would be general or sector specific. The US currently levies a general 12.5% tariff on Vietnamese goods that was imposed ‌in July after an investigation into alleged failures to ⁠prevent imports of goods made with forced labour.

Vietnam, long accused of being a transit hub for Chinese goods, faced 20% tariffs after Trump's "Liberation Day", which were struck down by the Supreme Court. Many economists ⁠have said the objective of the Trump administration is to reimpose at least the same level of tariffs that the Supreme Court abolished.

Electric car maker Tesla urged the US Trade Representative to "take into account the supply chain needs of American manufacturers". Some advanced components and precision manufacturing equipment cannot ​be sourced ​domestically despite major investments in US production, it said in comments sent ​on July 2.

Samsung's US unit made a similar argument, ‌noting Vietnam produces a significant share of Samsung's smartphones and network equipment for the US market. The South Korean company is Vietnam's largest foreign investor, having invested about $25 billion there.

Retail groups and trade associations representing industries with extensive manufacturing operations in Vietnam, including footwear, apparel and makers of consumer goods such as bikes or video game consoles, also opposed additional tariffs.

Vietnam's exports to US surged 42% in the first eight months of this year compared to the same period in 2025, making it the US trading partner with the ‌largest goods surplus ahead of China and Mexico. That compares with its position ​as the fourth-biggest at the end of 2025.

Story Continues

STEEL, SOLAR AND WOOD GROUPS ALLEGE ​UNFAIR PRACTICES

Industry groups representing US producers of steel, seafood, plywood, ​solar panels and wood products accused Vietnam of unfair practices and called for new tariffs.

Copyright holders such ‌as software, film and music industry groups urged Washington ​to secure concrete commitments from Vietnam ​to combat widespread piracy.

The Business Software Alliance, whose members include Microsoft , Oracle and IBM, said about three-quarters of software installed on personal computers in Vietnam was unlicensed, citing a 2017 survey. It criticised what it described as "inadequate enforcement", despite repeated ​commitments by Vietnam to address the issue.

The Motion ‌Picture Association said Vietnam was a major hub for online piracy, hosting websites distributing stolen film and television ​content that attracted over 12.5 billion visits worldwide last year. It called for stronger enforcement and improved market access ​for legitimate streaming services.

(Reporting by Francesco Guarascio; Editing by Edwina Gibbs)

news.Title: U.S. stock futures rise after bruising Oct; earnings, elections in focus
news.Content:
Investing.com-- U.S. stock index futures rose early-Monday, heralding some recovery on Wall Street after doubts over artificial intelligence spending sparked deep losses in technology valuations in October.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Focus is now squarely on more key earnings due this week, with Apple set to report on Monday while the midterm elections are scheduled for Tuesday.

Futures extended gains during the Asian session, as markets were also encouraged by a rebound in regional technology shares.

S&P 500 Futures rose 0.44% to 7,647.50 points, Nasdaq 100 Futures rose 0.87% to 28,782.0 points, and Dow Jones Futures rose 0.34% to 52,092.0 points by 01:47 ET (06:47 GMT).

Futures firmed after a deeply negative Friday session on Wall Street, which capped off a month of pronounced tech-driven losses in U.S. markets.

The NASDAQ Composite slid more than 5% in October, while the S&P 500 shed 0.9%. Flows out of tech and into more defensive sectors saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average add 1.7% in October.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Chipmakers and AI-exposed names were the worst performers, as a swathe of middling megacap tech earnings sparked increased questions over whether the hundreds of billions of dollars invested in the technology will bring adequate returns.

Several more major tech companies are set to report this week, with prints from iPhone maker Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL) and data firm Palantir Technologies Inc (NASDAQ:PLTR) due on Monday.

Hedge fund Berkshire Hathaway Inc (NYSE:BRKa) is also set to report on Monday, while chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices Inc (NASDAQ:AMD) will report on Tuesday.

The U.S. midterm elections are also on tap this week, and are broadly expected to set the tone for legislative policy over the remainder of President Donald Trump's second term.

Trump and the Republican party face a challenging backdrop going into the elections, amid growing voter discontent over high gasoline prices and a prolonged war with Iran.

A recent Reuters/IPSOS poll showed Trump's approval at a record-low 31%. All 435 seats in the House of Representatives, along with 35 Senate seats are on the ballot.

A Democrat majority in both levels of Congress presents a major hurdle to Trump and the Republicans in enacting more policies. A split Congress could also push the White House into relying more on executive measures for policy, which could keep uncertainty high for the remainder of Trump's term.

news.Title: If I Could Only Buy and Hold 1 "Magnificent Seven" Stock Through 2030, It Would Be This One
news.Content:
The "Magnificent Seven" is a cohort of big tech stocks that consists of:

Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA)

Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL)

Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT)

Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL)

Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN)

Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META)

Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA)

This group of stocks have led the market for a long time, and they are among the top 10 largest companies listed on U.S. exchanges. Each is also working on artificial intelligence technologies to some extent, but there are questions as to which stock will be the best performer through 2030. I think if you look at market commentary and what these companies are saying, the choice is obvious: Nvidia.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Nvidia should deliver the best returns through 2030, mostly thanks to the incredible growth it will take to get there. But how far could it go? Let's take a look.

Many companies in the Magnificent Seven are paying Nvidia billions of dollars

Nvidia makes GPUs , along with the software and other hardware to support their use. Graphics processing units are the top choice for many AI workloads, whether for training or inference. Nvidia's GPUs are generally recognized as best-in-class and have become synonymous with AI computing for a reason.

Many of the companies on this list are spending hundreds of billions of dollars on AI infrastructure each year . That figure goes to a handful of places, but purchasing computing units is by far the largest use of that capital. Because Nvidia is far larger than its competitors combined, it's the stock to own to capitalize on the AI build-out.

There are countless projections about AI spending through 2030, and all of them are mind-boggling. Nvidia's own projection estimates that global annual data center capital expenditures will reach $3 trillion to $4 trillion by 2030. That's simply astounding, but Nvidia is in a far better position to estimate it, given how far in advance customers are placing orders.

For example, during its Q2 earnings call, the company revealed it expects 70% revenue growth in 2027. Nvidia wouldn't have done that if management wasn't entirely confident in next year's sales, but because it is selling out production capacity, it's easy to estimate what future growth will be like.

Nvidia estimates that this year, the big five AI hyperscalers' capital expenditures will total nearly $800 billion. Next year, that figure is $1.3 trillion. With all the other AI firms around the world included, it's easy to see how spending will likely double between next year's estimates and 2030.

Story Continues

With that, we can see what kind of growth Nvidia can expect.

Nvidia will easily outpace the competition

If Nvidia's revenue growth is 70% in 2027, then doubles again from 2028 to 2030, that would yield a total growth of 240%. That's far faster than anything other members of the Magnificent Seven are putting up.

NVDA Revenue (Quarterly YoY Growth) data by YCharts

The next fastest-grower, Meta, is growing at a 26% clip. It would take Meta far longer to deliver this kind of return than it would for Nvidia, and it's almost impossible for any other stock to outperform over that time period simply because its growth will push it there.

I think that easily makes Nvidia the best buy among the Magnificent Seven, as its best years are still ahead. I think Nvidia is an excellent buy now, and if you've got some extra cash lying around, scooping it up now before it reports earnings near the end of November may be a smart idea. Nvidia's stock hasn't had the best year, and one good quarter could easily change that fact.

news.Title: Barclays Says a SpaceX Merger Is Now "a Key Part" of the Tesla Bull Case. Here's Who Actually Wins if It Happens -- and Who Pays.
news.Content:
In Space Exploration Technologies ' (NASDAQ: SPCX) recent third-quarter conference call, CEO Elon Musk was asked about the possibility of the company being merged with Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) -- his other trillion-dollar company. Musk responded by saying he thought merging the two companies was a good idea and confirmed that each company had formed a special committee to explore a potential combination of the businesses.

Long-running speculation that a potential merger between SpaceX and Tesla could be on the horizon has seemingly been confirmed, and it has now become an important part of the broader bullish case for Tesla. In a recent analyst note, Barclays highlighted the potential implications of a merger for Tesla shareholders.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Being acquired by SpaceX could benefit Tesla shareholders

SpaceX currently has a market capitalization of roughly $2 trillion. Meanwhile, Tesla has a market cap of roughly $1.55 trillion. SpaceX's larger size makes it more likely to be the acquirer in a potential merger with Tesla, and the companies' respective financial profiles, along with current difficulties securing large loans at favorable interest rates, suggest that an acquisition would be largely or entirely funded through stock. Musk's role as CEO of both companies and compensation-based incentives also suggest that SpaceX acquiring Tesla in a stock-heavy deal is the most likely outcome.

TSLA Market Cap data by YCharts

In Barclays' recent coverage of Tesla, lead analyst Dan Levy upgraded his rating on the stock from equal weight to overweight and raised his one-year price target from $370 to $450 per share. Not coincidentally, the analyst's price target of $450 per share matches his expectation for the equivalent value at which Tesla would be acquired in an all-stock deal.

At a buyout price of $450 per share, Tesla shareholders would receive a valuation premium of roughly 20% over the stock's current price. In other words, they would receive about 3.1 shares of SpaceX stock for every share of Tesla they currently own, based on each company's share price at the time of this writing.

In addition to clearing regulatory hurdles, a potential buyout hinges on approval from Tesla's shareholders. A deal would need to clear a 50% affirmative approval threshold. This means that investors who did not participate in the vote would have their equivalent voting shares tallied as "no" votes when determining whether the acquisition would proceed.

Story Continues

Musk currently controls roughly 20% of Tesla's voting power and could likely muster significant support from institutional investors. However, he would still likely need meaningful support from retail investors to close a deal. With that in mind, an even greater valuation premium may be offered to Tesla shareholders.

If an acquisition eventually goes through, buying Tesla stock today could be a way to purchase SpaceX stock at a substantial valuation discount. On the other hand, the heavy dilution stemming from the new stock offerings needed to fund a potential deal makes the outlook for SpaceX stock after a deal more difficult to predict. As it stands, a potential deal looks more heavily weighted in favor of Tesla shareholders.

news.Title: Google Just Lost Half a Trillion Dollars. It Has a Real Problem With Search Monetization.
news.Content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) has given investors plenty of growth to celebrate. Paying for that growth is becoming the harder part. The same technology that creates new cloud customers can also change how existing businesses earn their money. For shareholders, that means watching both sides of the ledger: What AI adds and what it puts at risk.

The industry's spending race already threatens returns across the AI supply chain. Google's latest quarter adds a more uncomfortable possibility, as building a better product could weaken the economics of the business financing it.

More News from Barchart

SpaceX Reportedly Faces Higher Borrowing Costs on Its $40 Billion GPU Deal. What It Means for SPCX Stock.

Why It's Time to Buy the Pullback in Alphabet Stock

SoFi Stock Is Ready for Its Next Big Move. Here's Why.

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL) lost roughly $500 billion in market value on Oct. 29 as GOOGL stock fell more than 12% to record its worst day ever. That wasn't cash disappearing from Google's bank account. It was investors slashing what they would pay for its future.

Google's AI Search Has a Revenue Problem

In Alphabet's third-quarter earnings release, Google Search and other revenue rose 12% to $63.35 billion. Search Engine Journal's comparison of its quarterly disclosures puts that growth below 17% in Q2 and 19% in Q1. Yet CEO Sundar Pichai said search-query growth reached its fastest pace in five years. So, people are searching more, but Search is experiencing slower revenue growth. That's the friction investors need to understand.

On the Oct. 28 earnings call, Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler acknowledged that AI Mode's lower monetization contributed to the slowdown. In other words, Google's expanding AI search experience hasn't yet developed the same advertising earning power investors expect from the Search business.

Granted, Schindler identified currency as the largest contributor to the deceleration, alongside advertising-category changes, so AI wasn't the whole explanation. His statement also doesn't quite prove that AI Overviews — the summaries feature above regular results — is causing paid clicks to collapse. AI Mode is a separate conversational experience. Management's acknowledgment supports a monetization concern; it hasn't proven yet that advertisers are seeing a decline in clicks because of AI.

Earlier research suggests fewer website visits need not hurt Google. SparkToro's analysis of Similarweb's January–April panel found 68% of searches generated no click, yet its comparison with earlier research showed a larger share of clicks going to ads. Different panels limit that comparison, but the implication is important: Publishers can lose traffic while Google keeps earning.

Story Continues

The latest earnings call raises a separate concern about whether rapidly growing AI Mode usage can generate enough advertising revenue.

The Spending Bill Keeps Growing

The timing makes that concern harder to shrug off. Alphabet's earnings release filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) shows $42.3 billion in Q3 operating cash flow against $51.4 billion in capital spending. Free cash flow was -$9.1 billion.

That spending sits alongside Google's expanding infrastructure financing commitments. Shareholders need advertising cash generation to remain dependable while those investments mature.

The cash squeeze extends beyond Google. In Q3, Amazon (AMZN) reported -$42.4 billion in trailing-12-month (TTM) free cash flow, attributing the deterioration primarily to increased AI investment.

But Google faces an additional challenge: Improving AI search economics while paying for the infrastructure supporting it.

Cloud Gives Bulls a Real Counterargument

Alphabet's AI gamble is also producing revenue, so it's not in danger of collapsing. Google Cloud revenue doubled in Q3, rising 103% year-over-year (YOY) to $30.7 billion. Cloud operating income reached $11.1 billion versus $3.6 billion a year earlier.

For comparison, Amazon's earnings release showed AWS revenue up 39% YOY to $46 billion. Google is growing faster from a smaller base, although its cloud growth also benefited from hardware sales.

Pichai described Google's strategy as developing the user experience before monetization. If advertising catches up, today's gap could prove temporary.

Still, AI infrastructure investments must eventually produce durable cash flow. Usage alone won't settle the investment case. The next few quarters need to show that Google's AI users can become profitable advertising customers without requiring ever-larger infrastructure checks. That's the test behind the headline loss.

Wall Street Remains Optimistic

While the stock decline didn't shake analyst sentiment in Alphabet's future — with the vast majority of the 53 analysts covering the company reiterating their "Buy" ratings — analysts at Citigroup and Citizens JMP both downgraded GOOG stock to a "Market Perform" rating from "Market Outperfom." Meanwhile, JPMorgan Chase analyst Douglas Anmuth lowered his price target from $425 to $375 while keeping an "Overweight" rating. UBS analyst Stephen Ju also reiterated a reduce recommendation.

Key Takeaway

Google's AI gamble hasn't failed, but its search monetization problem is real. Existing shareholders have reason to hold while cloud profits grow. Prospective buyers should demand improving search revenue growth and free cash flow before treating the selloff as a bargain.

The impact of AI on monetization is still evolving. Investors would do well to see whether this quarter was a one-off, or if this will be a recurring theme. That's not just for Alphabet, either. With tech stock valuations trading at premium levels, investors can't afford for the biscuit wheels on AI's gravy train to suddenly derail.

news.Title: SpaceX Stock Is Nearly 30% Below Its Post-IPO High. Here's What Facebook's Stock Did From the Same Spot.
news.Content:
SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) went public at $135 per share in June, and its stock set a record close of $201.80 on June 16, its third day of trading. At roughly $144 as I write, shares are about 29% below that peak.

Facebook, now Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META), has been in that spot. It spent long stretches of its first year as a public company a third or more below its own post-IPO high. And I think how it finally got out says a lot about what SpaceX shareholders might need to see.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Facebook's first year

Facebook priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $38 per share on May 17, 2012, and the stock closed its first day of trading at $38.23. That close was its high for over a year.

By June 5, the stock had closed at $25.87, around a third below the first-day close. It bounced into the low $30s later in June, then dropped to a closing low of $17.73 on Sept. 4 -- another 31% below the June 5 mark.

Then it rebounded, and by late November 2012, around three months after the bottom, Facebook was back near $26 -- again about a third below its high.

SpaceX has already followed the first half of that path. Its stock first closed over a third below the record on July 16, then dropped to a closing low of $108.27 on Aug. 5. Now, around three months past that low, it sits about where Facebook sat in late November 2012.

But Facebook didn't return to its high from there. The stock closed at $26.51 on July 24, 2013, almost exactly where it was eight months before, after rising as high as $32.47 in January and sliding to $22.90 in June.

One report moved Facebook's stock

Facebook's problem was specific. Its IPO filing warned that more use of its mobile products, "where we do not currently display ads," instead of PCs could hit revenue.

Showing how fast that problem was shrinking, mobile was 14% of Facebook's advertising revenue in the third quarter of 2012, around 23% in the fourth quarter, and about 30% in the first quarter of 2013. Next came the second-quarter 2013 report on July 24. Mobile had reached about 41% of ad revenue, and total revenue rose 53% year over year to $1.81 billion -- a pickup from 32% growth in the third quarter of 2012.

That report seemed to settle the doubt. The stock jumped around 30% the next day, and within two weeks it had passed its $38 IPO price and hit a new closing high.

Story Continues

What does Facebook's path say about SpaceX?

The most useful lesson, I think, is about patience. A stock that bounces off its low can go nowhere for months, even as revenue rises quickly.

But the two companies are very different. Facebook earned most of its money from ads, and its doubt boiled down to one number, mobile's share of ad revenue. SpaceX runs rocket launches, the Starlink satellite internet service, and an artificial intelligence (AI) arm that rents out computing power and sells AI software and ads -- now its largest segment by revenue.

SpaceX is also growing much faster, with third-quarter revenue up 161% year over year to $14.6 billion. But it's spending on a scale Facebook never did. Purchases of property, plant, and equipment were $48.1 billion in the first nine months of 2026, against $13.1 billion in operating cash flow. Facebook, in contrast, produced around $1.4 billion in free cash flow in the first half of 2013.

For SpaceX, the doubt is whether the AI spending pays off. Management expects first-quarter 2027 revenue of $33 billion to $37 billion, over twice the third quarter's. Of course, CEO Elon Musk said SpaceX rents its computing power at "effectively the spot-market rate," so that revenue may swing with rental prices.

At about $144, SpaceX is worth roughly $2 trillion, or about 14 times sales if the first-quarter range holds for a full year. It's arguably a fair price for a company growing so fast, though only if the guidance lands.

Ultimately, Facebook's first year suggests a third below the high can be a long place to wait, and the wait ended only when the business answered its biggest doubt. But it can't say when SpaceX gets its answer, or if it'll be a good one.

I wouldn't buy SpaceX shares because Facebook finally recovered. What would move me is SpaceX posting first-quarter 2027 revenue in management's range.

news.Title: Dear ON Semiconductor Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 2
news.Content:
ON Semiconductor (ON), commonly known as Onsemi, will report its third-quarter fiscal 2026 results on Nov. 2 after the market closes. Ahead of the report, the company has also landed a lucrative revised acquisition deal.

In June, Onsemi struck a deal to acquire fabless chip firm Synaptics (SYNA) for $7 billion in an all-stock transaction, which caused ON stock to drop sharply as investors feared dilution. However, in October, the company amended the deal to a $123-per-share cash deal for an aggregate value of approximately $5.7 billion. In addition to a lower price tag, the all-cash deal means no dilution for ON stock shareholders. Meanwhile, the company is also reportedly eyeing a purchase of startup chip firm Ferric for approximately $1 billion.

More News from Barchart

Why It's Time to Buy the Pullback in Alphabet Stock

ORCL Stock Has a Solid Base to Build on After Q1, Especially as Oracle Announces Key AI Partnerships

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

Therefore, all eyes will be on Onsemi's cash position with the upcoming quarterly report.

About ON Semiconductor Stock

ON Semiconductor is a global semiconductor company headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona. The company makes chips that manage power and sense things such as images, helping cars, factories, data centers, and everyday electronics use energy more safely and efficiently. The company designs, manufactures, and sells products worldwide, with a strong focus on automotive and industrial markets. Onsemi has a market capitalization of $27.9 billion.

ON stock is up 41% over the past 52 weeks, mainly because investors see improving growth and a stronger position in artificial intelligence (AI) power, electric vehicles (EVs), and energy storage. However, ON stock is down 29% over the past six months because investors have become more worried about near-term demand in the company's biggest markets, especially cars and industrial equipment. The stock reached a 52-week high of $134.92 on June 3 but is currently down 47% from that level.

Meanwhile, the forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 23.4 times is slightly higher than the industry average of 22.1 times.

Q2 Earnings Beat Expectations as AI and Auto Demand Lifted Revenue Growth

For the second quarter, Onsemi's revenue increased 9% year-over-year (YOY) to $1.6 billion, surpassing the $1.59 billion that Wall Street analysts had expected.

Story Continues

Growth in the Power Solutions Group (PSG) led the results, with the segment's top line growing 19% YOY to $829 million. PSG contains the company's AI data-center and high-voltage power businesses, which saw the strongest demand.

Automotive demand also raised Intelligent Sensing Group (ISG) revenue by 7% YOY to $228.8 million. This segment contains the company's CMOS image sensors, SPAD, and SiPM technologies used heavily in automotive safety and industrial applications.

Onsemi's non-GAAP operating margin grew from 17.3% to 20.8% over the same period. Non-GAAP EPS also grew 40% YOY to $0.74, topping the $0.72 analysts expected. Importantly, free cash flow margin expanded from about 7% to 27%, giving the company more money to reinvest in its business and carry out acquisitions.

Wall Street is robustly optimistic about Onsemi's future earnings. Analysts expect EPS to climb 40% YOY to $0.88 in Q3. For fiscal 2026, EPS is projected to surge 37% YOY to $3.21, followed by 40% YOY growth to $4.50 in fiscal 2027.

What Do Analysts Think About ON Semiconductor Stock?

In October, B. Riley lowered its price target for ON stock from $127 to $105 while keeping a "Buy" rating. Following Texas Instruments' (TXN) report, analysts see a sustained analog semiconductor upcycle into 2027. However, analysts also believe recent sector share price gains have compressed valuation multiples.

Susquehanna analyst Christopher Rolland also recently lowered his price target from $150 to $120 while keeping a "Positive" rating on the stock. Susquehanna expects "modest upside" from the company's Q3 results and Q4 guidance, with AI trends and a broader semiconductor upcycle driving improvement.

Last month, StoneX also initiated coverage of Onsemi with a "Buy" rating and a $110 price target. StoneX believes the company is positioned to benefit from broadening chip cycle strength.

Overall, Onsemi is gaining praise on Wall Street, with analysts awarding ON stock a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating. Of the 30 analysts covering the stock, 11 have a "Strong Buy" rating, two analysts have a "Moderate Buy," and 17 have a "Hold" rating. The average price target of $99.88 represents potential upside of 39% from current levels, while the Street-high price target of $137 implies 91% potential upside from here.

news.Title: Why It's Time to Buy the Pullback in Alphabet Stock
news.Content:
Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL) shares fell sharply after the company's Q3 earnings announcement, plunging more than 12% in a single day and wiping billions of dollars from its market capitalization. The decline was driven mainly by slower-than-expected growth in Google Search and concerns about the company's rapidly escalating investments in artificial intelligence (AI).

Google Search, Alphabet's largest revenue-generating segment, delivered revenue of $63.3 billion, up about 12% year-over-year (YoY). This marked a deceleration from the 17% growth reported in Q2 and fell short of Wall Street expectations. Although challenging YoY comparisons contributed to the moderation, investors were particularly concerned about the slowdown occurring alongside a substantial increase in AI-related spending.

More News from Barchart

SpaceX Reportedly Faces Higher Borrowing Costs on Its $40 Billion GPU Deal. What It Means for SPCX Stock.

ORCL Stock Has a Solid Base to Build on After Q1, Especially as Oracle Announces Key AI Partnerships

SoFi Stock Is Ready for Its Next Big Move. Here's Why.

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

The slowdown raises concerns over whether Alphabet can generate sufficient returns from its aggressive AI investments to justify the associated costs. During Q3, capital expenditures reached $51.4 billion, with most of the spending directed toward the technical infrastructure required to support AI. While these investments could strengthen Alphabet's competitive positioning and create new monetization opportunities over the longer term, their near-term impact on profitability and cash generation remains a concern.

The pressure on cash flows is already becoming evident. Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion in Q3, reflecting the substantial financial burden associated with expanding its technical infrastructure and building inventory of Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) systems as it scales its AI-related operations. Continued investment at this pace could constrain free cash flow in the coming quarters.

Near-term challenges are also likely to persist. Google Search faces tough year-over-year (YoY) comparisons in Q4, which could make it difficult to reaccelerate reported growth. At the same time, elevated capital expenditure requirements may continue to restrict free cash flow.

Why Buy GOOGL Stock?

Despite near-term headwinds, including concerns over moderating Search growth and elevated capital expenditure, Alphabet's long-term investment outlook remains solid. The company's strong positioning in AI, accelerating Google Cloud growth, and expanding the subscription ecosystem provide multiple avenues for sustained revenue expansion. Against this backdrop, the recent share price correction presents an attractive entry opportunity for investors with a long-term investment horizon.

Story Continues

A key driver of Alphabet's growth is the accelerating momentum in Google Cloud, supported by growing enterprise demand for AI-related infrastructure and solutions. In the latest quarter, Cloud revenue surged 103% YoY to $30.7 billion, reflecting robust performance across AI infrastructure, AI solutions, and core Google Cloud Platform (GCP) offerings. Growth also accelerated from the previous quarter, highlighting improving momentum. Moreover, sales of its TPU systems have become a meaningful contributor.

Google Cloud's backlog reached $561 billion in the third quarter, and management expects to recognize slightly more than 55% of it as revenue over the next 24 months. The sizeable backlog provides considerable revenue visibility.

Alphabet's AI ecosystem is also gaining traction. The Gemini application has reached 1 billion users, making it the fastest-growing product in the company's history. This growing adoption strengthens Alphabet's position in the increasingly competitive AI market and creates opportunities to monetize its AI capabilities across consumer and enterprise offerings.

Meanwhile, the subscription business is providing an additional source of growth and diversification beyond advertising. Subscription, Platforms, and Devices revenue increased 11% YoY to $14.3 billion, driven by strong demand for YouTube subscriptions, particularly YouTube Music and YouTube Premium, as well as growing adoption of AI-powered plans within Google One. Continued expansion of subscription revenue is strategically important because it broadens Alphabet's revenue mix and reduces its dependence on advertising over time.

Overall, although Google Search faces challenging comparisons and AI-related investments are likely to keep capital expenditure elevated, Alphabet's accelerating Cloud business, expanding AI ecosystem, and resilient subscription operations provide compelling long-term growth drivers. These businesses could help offset moderation in Search growth and support continued revenue diversification. Consequently, the recent pullback offers a favorable opportunity to buy GOOGL stock at a better price.

Analysts remain bullish, with a "Strong Buy" consensus rating on GOOGL shares, reflecting continued optimism about the company's growth potential.

news.Title: Apple to report Q4 earnings Monday, with iPhone 18 sales in the spotlight
news.Content:
Apple ( AAPL ) will report its fourth quarter earnings after the bell Monday, providing investors with a glimpse of early iPhone 18 Pro sales.

The iPhone Duo went up for preorder on Oct. 16 and went on sale Oct. 23, missing Apple's fiscal Q4, though the company could still offer color on demand.

This will also be Apple's first earnings call with new CEO John Ternus , who took over the role from Tim Cook on Sept. 1.

For the quarter, Apple is expected to report earnings per share (EPS) of $2 on revenue of $113.46 billion, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus estimates. The company saw EPS of $1.85 and revenue of $102.46 billion in the same period last year.

Apple's iPhone sales are projected to hit $56.48 billion, up 15% year over year. Services, the company's second-largest segment, is set to top $31.58 billion in revenue, while the company's Mac business is expected to see sales of $9.69 billion.

Wearables and iPad should generate $8.99 billion and $6.83 billion, respectively.

Apple stock has been a relative safe haven among tech stocks this year. Shares of the iPhone maker are up roughly 30% over the past 12 months. Peers Amazon ( AMZN ), Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and Nvidia ( NVDA ) are up single digits in the same period, while Microsoft ( MSFT ) stock is flat. Shares of Meta ( META ) are down about 15%.

The last month hasn't been any better. Google, Meta, and Nvidia took major hits, declining double digits. Google and Meta got dinged following their earnings results, and Nvidia is at least partly a victim of fears about the AI trade. Amazon is also off slightly over the past month, leaving just Apple and Microsoft in the green.

Apple has been largely insulated from the highs and lows of the AI market. It doesn't spend billions on data centers, and it doesn't rely on chip sales to generate revenue.

And that's been a big help for the company's stock price. Earlier this month, Apple's market capitalization eclipsed the $5 trillion mark for the second time . Nvidia is the only other company to reach the milestone.

Apple is also riding a wave of new product launches. Outside of the iPhone 18 Pros and iPhone Duo, Apple has debuted a new pair of AirPods, Apple Watches, Macs, iPads, and more. Earlier this week, the company released an upgraded iPad mini, an improved iMac, and more powerful MacBook Pros , including one with a touchscreen display .

And earlier this month, it debuted its first smart home hub , the Apple HomeView .

Apple's next major releases are expected early next year and will include a base iPhone 18 and a follow-up to the iPhone Air.
