news.Title: After Meta, Could These Be Wall Street’s Next Blockbuster Stock Splits?
news.Content:
Could stock-split mania take over Wall Street in the next few years? On the one hand, many corporations are capitalizing on artificial intelligence (AI) and have seen their share prices soar, potentially triggering a wave of blockbuster stock splits. And one could also argue that Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) just kicked things off by announcing a 2-for-1 stock split that will create a brand-new category of non-voting shares.

That will allow the tech leader to issue shares to finance its AI-related ambitions without reducing the voting power of its CEO, Mark Zuckerberg.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

However, it is always hard to predict upcoming stock splits, even if some signs point in that direction. That said, if there are more stock splits on the horizon, here are two companies that could join the club: Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) and MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI).

Image source: The Motley Fool.

1. Micron Technology

Micron Technology designs and sells computer memory chips. Demand for the company's products has soared amid the massive ongoing AI build-out, and the semiconductor specialist is reaping the benefits. Micron's revenue and net income have reached all-time highs.

MU Revenue (Annual) data by YCharts

What's more, the AI tailwind could be far from over. Not only are Micron's chips in high demand, but there is also a severe shortage, giving it significant pricing power. Consider, for instance, that Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) increased its capex guidance for 2026 from $200 billion to $220 billion, partly due to higher memory chip prices. Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), another hyperscaler, also attributed some of its massive capex guidance for the year to rising memory chip prices. This helps highlight the scale of the opportunity for Micron.

Further, the shortage of memory chips might last at least a couple more years. Micron's shares have gained significant value this year on the back of excellent financial results, and despite a pullback in recent months, the company's prospects remain bright.

Shares are currently changing hands for about $983 apiece. Of course, there is no generally agreed-upon price at which a company must split its stock. Still, if Micron performs well over the next year or two and continues to capitalize on the soaring demand for its products, the company could decide to split its stock.

Story Continues

It has done so before, but the last time was in 2000 -- another reason why the time may be ripe for a stock split. Even if management doesn't announce one, Micron's position in the memory chip market and the industry's rapid growth make it an attractive stock to buy and hold.

2. MercadoLibre

MercadoLibre has faced challenges over the past year. Stiff competition in the e-commerce market in Latin America is forcing the company to make business investments that are harming short-term profits. MercadoLibre's shares have lagged broader equities as a result. However, the stock remains fairly expensive.

As of writing, shares are trading at about $1,673 each. Besides, MercadoLibre could bounce back in the medium term as the company's investments start to pay off. MercadoLibre has extended free shipping offers across various markets.

This can attract more customers and even increase purchase amounts per customer. That can potentially mean higher gross merchandise volume and revenue for the e-commerce specialist. The company is also doubling down on its banking ambitions, another attractive growth avenue, since many people in the regions it serves remain underbanked.

The short-term hit to profits is worth the investment, especially since MercadoLibre operates in a region with one of the fastest rates of e-commerce growth in recent years. The company boasts a wide moat from network effects and switching costs which, together with its investments, could allow it to ride this tailwind. And if the share price grows significantly over the next few years, MercadoLibre could opt for a stock split.

True, the company has never conducted a stock split, and management may keep things that way. Whatever MercadoLibre decides, though, it's worth sticking with the company for the long term. Thankfully, plenty of online trading platforms offer fractional shares.

news.Title: 5 Most Profitable Stocks of the Past 5 Years
news.Content:
Profitability has become increasingly concentrated among companies controlling the infrastructure, software, and platforms supporting the digital economy, and investors are increasingly looking towards the most profitable stocks of the past five years to make sense of the ongoing market trends. Artificial intelligence has accelerated this trend, creating enormous demand for advanced semiconductors, memory chips, and cloud computing capacity. Meanwhile, digital advertising, enterprise software, consumer technology, and financial services continue to generate substantial earnings through established customer relationships and recurring revenue.

The semiconductor industry has emerged as a particularly significant beneficiary. Companies such as NVIDIA, Micron, and SK hynix are capitalizing on demand for AI computing and memory, while Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company profits from manufacturing the advanced chips used across the industry. However, these businesses are exposed to different risks. Memory manufacturers depend heavily on supply and pricing conditions, while chip designers must sustain demand for increasingly expensive computing systems. Check out our list of the 10 Oversold AI Stocks: Where Wall Street Analysts Are Spotting 50%+ Upside .

Cloud computing presents a different financial equation. Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet are generating substantial revenue from businesses purchasing digital infrastructure, but expanding their computing capacity requires enormous investment. According to Reuters, second-quarter S&P 500 earnings were on track to increase 52% year over year in 2026, supported by a 74% profit jump in the technology ‌sector. This is compared with 33% when substantial investment-related gains were excluded, according to Tajinder Dhillon, head of earnings research at LSEG. The difference illustrates why reported net income does not always reflect recurring operating profitability. Also take a look at the 10 Stocks You Are Selling and Insiders Are Buying .

For investors, high earnings also do not necessarily make a stock attractive. A company can continue increasing profits while delivering disappointing shareholder returns if its valuation already assumes even faster growth. Conversely, companies with more modest earnings growth may offer attractive opportunities when expectations are sufficiently restrained.

With this backdrop, we present the expanded list of the 10 Most Profitable Stocks of the Past 5 Years here . You can see the top 5 stocks below.

Story Continues

Our Methodology

For this list, we shortlisted stocks listed on US exchanges and calculated their cumulative net income over five years using Yahoo Finance's Net Income figures. We added annual net income for fiscal 2022 through 2026 where available, using trailing twelve-month (TTM) net income as an approximation for 2026. Since TTM periods can overlap with previously reported annual results, these totals are estimates.

For foreign companies, we converted earnings into US dollars using Yahoo Finance exchange rates. The stocks are also popular among analysts and elite hedge funds, according to Insider Monkey's Q2 2026 database, and are arranged in ascending order of their cumulative net income.

Why do we care about what hedge funds do? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Our quarterly newsletter's strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612.3% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ).

10 Most Profitable Stocks of the Past 5 Years

5. Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN )

5-Year Net Income: $299.91 billion

Number of Hedge Funds: 369

Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) generates income across e-commerce, advertising, and cloud computing, but Amazon Web Services (AWS) plays a disproportionately important role in operating profitability. In the second quarter of 2026, AWS generated $16.6 billion of Amazon's $27.5 billion in operating income, illustrating how its cloud business contributes more to earnings than its revenue share might suggest. AWS segment sales increased 37% to $42.2 billion, supported by demand for computing capacity and AI infrastructure.

However, Amazon's reported net income requires an important qualification. Second-quarter earnings included $53.4 billion in non-operating pretax income, primarily associated with its investment in Anthropic. Such gains do not necessarily represent recurring business profitability.

AWS offers opportunities for continued operating income growth. Reuters reported that its contracted backlog had reached $496 billion, providing visibility into future demand. Factors like these place Amazon first among our list of the best big name stocks according to financial media .

Nevertheless, expanding AI infrastructure has pushed Amazon's free cash flow into negative territory. The company burned $7.6 billion of cash on a trailing 12-month basis in fiscal Q2, compared to $18.2 billion in free cash flow a year earlier. Future profitability will depend on turning its substantial infrastructure commitments into sustainable operating returns and not just on investment revaluations.

4. Berkshire Hathaway Inc. (NYSE: BRK-B )

5-Year Net Income: $315.20 billion

Number of Hedge Funds: 135

Berkshire Hathaway Inc. (NYSE:BRK-B) more than doubled its net earnings in the second quarter of 2026, but the increase was not matched by comparable growth in its operating businesses. Nearly half of its reported profit came from investment gains, while operating earnings rose to $12.983 billion, supported by stronger performance outside insurance. Its cumulative net income reflects both business earnings and investment gains, including changes in the market value of its equity holdings.

However, insurance underwriting earnings declined to $1.731 billion from $1.992 billion, illustrating how profitability can face pressure even when overall operating results improve. Berkshire's investment portfolio also introduces an important distinction for shareholders. Unrealized gains can substantially increase reported net income without generating corresponding operating cash flow, while market declines can reduce earnings even when its underlying businesses remain profitable.

For shareholders, the more meaningful measure of Berkshire's performance is whether growth across its operating businesses can offset weakness in insurance while its accumulated capital is deployed productively.

3. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT )

5-Year Net Income: $468.78 billion

Number of Hedge Funds: 273

Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) has maintained strong profitability through its combination of enterprise software subscriptions and expanding cloud infrastructure. While Microsoft 365 provides recurring revenue, Azure has become a major source of growth as businesses increase spending on cloud computing and artificial intelligence.

The company's latest results demonstrate that this demand is translating into operating profits. Azure revenue increased 48% to $33.17 billion in the September 2026 quarter, while operating income rose 21%. Microsoft also generated $18.6 billion in free cash flow despite substantial infrastructure investments, exceeding analyst expectations by around $10 billion, according to Reuters.

Microsoft's $677 billion in commercial remaining performance obligations provides visibility into future revenue, although these contracts will be recognized over different periods. Management also expects Azure revenue growth of 49%–50% in the following quarter, which exceeds analyst estimates ​of 47.6%, according to Reuters.

However, the company's $45.2 billion in quarterly capital expenditure highlights the growing costs of supporting AI demand. Furthermore, reported net income growth of 32% partly reflected investment-related accounting effects, compared with 18% growth on an adjusted basis.

2. Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL )

5-Year Net Income: $531.48 billion

Number of Hedge Funds: 169

Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) continues to generate substantial earnings from its iPhone business, supported by an expanding services ecosystem that generates revenue beyond the initial hardware purchase. The combination enables Apple to benefit from both device sales and recurring spending across its installed customer base.

Services have become particularly important to Apple's profitability as the company balances hardware demand with higher-margin digital offerings. In its fiscal third quarter of 2026, services revenue increased 12.1% to $30.74 billion, while iPhone sales rose 21.7% to $54.25 billion, exceeding the $53.86 billion estimate.

Nevertheless, Apple's earnings growth faces constraints beyond consumer demand. Management has warned that shortages related to high-end processors and memory components are limiting its ability to meet demand, and that these shortages may affect both sales volumes and production costs.

Chief Financial Officer Kevan Parekh told analysts on a call that the company forecast revenue growth of 9% to 11% for its September quarter, below analysts' expectations of 12% at the time. Factors like these place AAPL among our list of the best big name stocks according to financial media .

Continued services expansion and hardware demand provide opportunities for higher income, but Apple's ability to convert that demand into earnings will depend partly on supply availability and maintaining profitability across its product portfolio.

1. Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL )

5-Year Net Income: $601.75 billion

Number of Hedge Funds: 275

Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) leads this ranking, supported by Google's highly profitable advertising operations and rapidly expanding cloud business. Search and YouTube continue generating substantial earnings, while demand for AI infrastructure is strengthening Google Cloud's contribution to operating income.

Google Cloud's operating income more than tripled to $11.12 billion in the September 2026 quarter, as revenue increased by a record 103% to $30.71 billion, supported by solid growth in Google Cloud Platform across enterprise AI solutions and enterprise AI infrastructure, along with core GCP services.

However, Alphabet's exceptionally high reported profitability requires qualification. Its latest quarter included an $8.66 billion loss on equity securities, contrasting with substantial investment gains earlier in 2026. These fluctuations make reported net income less representative of recurring operating performance.

According to Reuters, Alphabet's quarterly free cash flow was negative $9.07 billion, with an increase in capital spending and a slowdown in core ad business growth. For more comparative insight on how Alphabet compares with other popular stocks, read our insightful article on Microsoft vs. Alphabet: Is GOOGL's Cloud Growth Worth More Than Investors Think?

The company's $561 billion cloud backlog provides visibility into future demand, but does not guarantee equivalent earnings growth. Sustaining profitability will depend on converting cloud contracts into operating income while managing infrastructure costs and maintaining advertising growth amid competition in AI-powered search.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of GOOGL as an investment, we believe certain AI infrastructure stocks offer far stronger long-term potential at a much more attractive entry point. news.Title: Microsoft just gave Nvidia shareholders a reason to pay attention
news.Content: Nvidia has been one of the biggest winners of the AI boom, but its stock has cooled off as investors fret that Big Tech is overspending on data centers. The shares climbed more than 1,200% over the past three calendar years, yet they're up only about 13% so far in 2026. The stock has at least held up better than most. When AI and chip stocks lost more than $1 trillion in combined value during one week in mid-October, Nvidia fared better than many of its peers. Now one of its biggest customers has offered a fresh reason for optimism. Microsoft's latest report showed where its AI money is going, and much of it is landing on chips. Microsoft's spending tilts heavily toward chips Microsoft reported its fiscal first-quarter results on October 28, posting revenue of $92.3 billion, up 19% from a year earlier, while its Azure cloud business grew 48%, according to Microsoft . Net income rose 32% to $36.6 billion. Strong cloud demand like that is exactly what keeps chip orders flowing. Also read: Nvidia has a stake in SpaceX that came from an unexpected place The detail that matters most for Nvidia came in the spending breakdown. Roughly three-quarters of Microsoft's $45.2 billion in quarterly capex went toward "short-lived assets," a group that includes CPUs, GPUs, and data center networking gear. That works out to roughly $34 billion in a single quarter, much of it on the kind of hardware Nvidia sells. Microsoft isn't easing off, either. The company expects capex to top $50 billion in the second quarter and has guided for about $170 billion in calendar-year spending, with the increase driven by CPUs and GPUs. It also said it expects to remain cash-flow positive. Microsoft is spending because customers keep asking for more. Capex, including finance leases, actually came in a bit below analyst forecasts, yet the company guided for Azure growth of 49% to 50% next quarter and said Copilot users jumped 50% from the prior quarter, SiliconANGLE reported . "We still have demand that exceeds supply," chief financial officer Amy Hood said. Why this matters so much for Nvidia Nvidia leans heavily on customers like Microsoft. In its fiscal second quarter, Nvidia's revenue more than doubled to $96.2 billion, and its data center business brought in $89 billion of that, up 117% from a year earlier, according to Nvidia . That means data centers account for about 92% of total sales. Net income rose 126% to $59.7 billion. That concentration cuts both ways. Strong cloud spending can send Nvidia's results soaring, but any pullback by the biggest buyers would hit it hard. That's why investors pore over every capex update from Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta. Story Continues The near-term outlook looks solid. Nvidia has guided third-quarter revenue to about $108 billion, give or take 2%, without counting any data centre compute sales to China, as reported by Nvidia . Its next report, due in November, will show whether Big Tech's spending is still flowing through to its top line. The CPU angle adds another wrinkle. Nvidia recently launched its first stand-alone CPU, called Vera, built specifically to power AI agent workloads. If Microsoft's spending on CPUs keeps rising, Nvidia now has a product to compete for a share of that money too. The AI spending fears haven't gone away Not every tech giant got the same reception this week. Alphabet's shares fell about 10% after hours following a disappointing search business and negative free cash flow, while Microsoft rose more than 5% partly due to positive free cash flow. Even so, Alphabet plans to lift 2027 capital spending above this year's $195 billion to $205 billion forecast, which is more good news for chip suppliers. The split shows what investors want now. Capital.com analyst Daniela Hathorn said the Alphabet and Microsoft results offered "competing narratives" on whether AI is paying off. Spending alone no longer earns applause. Companies have to show it's turning into revenue. The bigger picture still favours chipmakers. Goldman Sachs expects the five largest U.S. hyperscalers to lift AI infrastructure spending to $1.2 trillion in 2027, up from roughly $800 billion this year, according to TheStreet . Its model shows capex growth stepping down to 54% in 2027 and just 12% in 2028. The bank also estimates these companies need about $300 billion in yearly AI revenue just to break even. More Microsoft: Microsoft's $665 target hinges on a new AI advantage Meta and Microsoft just sent employees a memo about Anthropic Microsoft just sent a strong message to Anthropic Other big customers are lining up too. Elon Musk said SpaceX's new computing capacity next year will be mostly Nvidia's Vera Rubin chips, and Jensen Huang has pointed to at least $1 trillion in orders for Blackwell and Vera Rubin through 2027. What it means for Nvidia shareholders The stock has lagged its own business. Nvidia gained 239% in 2023, 171% in 2024 and 39% in 2025, but its forward price-to-earnings ratio had fallen to about 23.2 by July, trading near parity with the S&P 500. That's a sharp change from years of trading at a steep premium. Microsoft's numbers suggest the spending story is still intact. One of Nvidia's largest customers put about three-quarters of its quarterly capex into chips and networking gear and plans to spend about $170 billion in fiscal 2027, according to Microsoft . With commitments like that on the table, it's hard to argue that demand is drying up anytime soon. There are risks. Nvidia depends on a small group of very large buyers, and many of them are now borrowing to fund the build-out. Morgan Stanley estimates AI-related global debt issuance will approach $570 billion in 2026, as reported by TheStreet . But for now, Microsoft is giving Nvidia shareholders exactly what they hoped to hear: the money is still flowing toward chips. news.Title: 3 Numbers to Watch to Know if Meta Platforms' AI Spending Is Paying Off
news.Content:
Mark Zuckerberg, Meta Platforms ' (NASDAQ: META) founder and CEO, views artificial intelligence (AI) as a generational opportunity. Therefore, the spending seems to have no upper limit, with $135 billion to $145 billion planned in capital expenditures (capex) in 2026. That number will surely be much higher next year.

The company's operating margin was cut in half to 20% last quarter (Q3 2026 ended Sept. 30), dropping from 40% in the year-ago period. Moreover, the business reported negative free cash flow (FCF) of $2.1 billion during Q3. These trends underscore the need to be more critical of the direction the social media giant is heading as it embarks on what might be a long-term capex spree.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Here are three metrics investors should watch to gauge whether Meta Platforms' AI spending is paying off.

1. Advertising revenue

Meta's 3.64 billion daily active users lay the foundation for one of the world's most powerful ecosystems. The business has the attention of 44% of the world's population. This setup enables the company to generate substantial digital advertising revenue . That's the first metric to keep tabs on.

So far, AI capabilities are driving better engagement. On the other hand, AI capabilities are helping advertisers run better, higher-return campaigns.

This is showing up in the numbers, although it's impossible to know how much is directly attributable to AI enhancements compared to the trajectory Meta Platforms was already on before this technology penetrated the economy. Ad revenue climbed 25.9% year over year last quarter. That gain was supported by a 10% and 14% growth in impressions and pricing, respectively.

Zuckerberg previously said that if the business delivers on its AI ambitions, advertising will represent a larger share of global GDP. Monetizing social media activity will remain the crown jewel operation. And AI must directly impact the company's ad platform.

2. New products and services

On Sept. 8, Meta Platforms launched its Muse AI agent . It has been a huge hit so far. It counted 10 million users in the U.S. and Canada a month and a half after its release. Perhaps more noteworthy is that 25% of these people use it daily.

Unlike other hyperscalers with massive cloud computing platforms, Meta historically hasn't had an immediate distribution channel to monetize its AI investments. Besides the ad ecosystem mentioned, the company is working on entirely new products and services designed with AI in mind from the start.

Story Continues

The Muse personal agent is one example. Another significant recent launch is Muse Wonder, Meta Platforms' first frontier model. There's also the Meta Enterprise Platform, which offers AI tools to corporate clients.

The question going forward is about monetization. Will these new products and services contribute meaningful revenue within the next five or 10 years? Investors should be watching this closely to gauge the success of Meta Platforms' sizable AI spending.

3. Operating cash flow

Because the company is investing so much in AI, it's critical not to just look at the income statement. I noted that Meta Platforms posted a FCF loss of $2.1 billion in the most recent quarter. This metric focuses attention on the cash flow statement. To get a clearer picture of the true economics, investors need to look here.

Watch operating cash flow (OCF) trends closely. Through the first nine months of 2026, this figure was up 21.7% year over year. In a vacuum, this is a strong gain.

However, it lagged the 72% growth in capex over the same period. Meta Platforms' spending is rising at a faster clip than OCF. As long as this continues, it will continue to burn cash.

The ideal scenario is that OCF eventually outpaces capex, supporting a return to positive FCF. But this might be far off, as the business just announced a plan to raise almost $100 billion in equity capital to fund the AI build-out. Investors will have to be patient for the payoff.

news.Title: SK hynix's Solidigm Is Mulling a $45 Billion Chip Plant Investment. What This Means for SKHY Stock.
news.Content:
Memory major SK hynix's (SKHY) subsidiary, Solidigm, is contemplating an investment of $45 billion to build a NAND manufacturing plant, according to Bloomberg . Acquired by SK hynix exactly six years ago from Intel (INTC) for $9 billion, Solidigm specializes in NAND flash memory and enterprise solid-state drives (SSDs).

A supposed angle to the investment involves Solidigm seeking concessions from the U.S. government to send additional semiconductor manufacturing equipment to the former's facility in Dalian, China. Meanwhile, the proposed facility is expected to be set up in Upstate New York. However, neither SK hynix nor Solidigm has officially confirmed this.

More News from Barchart

What to Expect From AMD's Q3 Earnings

SpaceX Reportedly Faces Higher Borrowing Costs on Its $40 Billion GPU Deal. What It Means for SPCX Stock.

ASML vs. Applied Materials: One Is Growing Twice as Fast, but I'd Buy The Other Instead

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

About SK hynix

SK hynix traces its origins to 1983 and was founded by Chung Ju-yung, the well-known founder of the Hyundai Group. Now under the ownership of the SK Group, the company ranks among the world's largest producers of semiconductor memory. Long established as a major force in DRAM and NAND flash memory, SK hynix has emerged as one of the primary beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence expansion thanks to its strong position in high-bandwidth memory chips that power AI accelerators, including Nvidia graphics processing units. The firm is widely viewed as the technology leader in the high-bandwidth memory segment and holds a strategically critical role within the global artificial intelligence supply chain.

With its ADRs listed on July 10, 2026, on the Nasdaq, the company currently commands a market cap of $1.4 trillion. Notably, the ADRs recently witnessed a pop of 13.3% following record quarterly results. Each ADR represents one-tenth of an ordinary share of the company.

But what role can Solidigm's proposed investment play in SK hynix's broader strategy? Let's find out.

Solid NAND

Prior to acquiring Solidigm, SK hynix's place in the NAND memory space was already well-established. However, what it was lacking was enterprise and data center storage capabilities. With Solidigm in its fold, that issue was resolved. What Solidigm brought to the table for SK hynix was an established SSD business, industry-leading NAND SSD technology, QLC NAND expertise, and the Dalian manufacturing facility in China.

Story Continues

Thus, SK hynix could combine its NAND manufacturing expertise with Intel's enterprise storage technology to compete more effectively in high-capacity SSDs used in data centers. SK hynix explicitly described this as an opportunity to strengthen its enterprise SSD capabilities, a market that is poised to reach a size of $111.29 billion by 2034, and in which SK hynix with Solidigm holds a 30.2% share, making it the second-largest player.

Meanwhile, the $45 billion expected investment would not be Solidigm's first in the country. Its first clearly announced investment initiative after its formation was a commitment to invest $100 million in research and development facilities in the Greater Sacramento region of California. The initiative focused on its headquarters in Rancho Cordova and the surrounding R&D campus. The aim was to strengthen its research capabilities, develop storage technologies, and expand its local workforce. This was strategically significant because Solidigm's business depends on developing increasingly dense, efficient, and high-capacity SSDs for enterprise customers. Research and development is therefore central to its competitiveness, particularly as AI data centers require more storage.

And this investment in R&D is leading to more product development that has the potential to not only solidify but also expand SK hynix's market share as well as challenge market leader Samsung. One of the key products is its 321-layer, 2-terabit QLC NAND. As per the company, compared with its previous QLC generation, the new technology doubled data-transfer speed, improved write performance by up to 56%, increased read performance by 18%, and improved write power efficiency by more than 23%.

Then, at Future of Memory and Storage 2026, SK hynix highlighted its PS1101 high-capacity enterprise SSD lineup, based on QLC NAND. The company said the product offered approximately 55% higher performance than the previous 176-layer generation and began sample shipments to major cloud service provider customers in August 2026.

Finally, the company also showcased 375-layer 4D NAND at the August 2026 event. Here, the technology uses wafer bonding and delivers 2.5 times the performance per watt of the previous generation. It also highlighted packaging technologies designed to increase density and improve space efficiency. Notably, SK hynix expects to begin mass production of high-performance enterprise SSDs based on this technology in the first half of 2027.

SK hynix's Record Q3

Having said that, SK hynix's latest results for Q3 2026 showcased a company that is firing on all cylinders, leading to a remarkable record-breaking showing.

The company saw quarterly sales surpassing 100 trillion won for the first time as revenues came in at 104.62 trillion won, a 32% growth from the previous year. DRAM continued to be the biggest revenue segment of the company at 75%, followed by NAND at 24%.

Operating profits followed a similar trajectory, growing by 38% in the same period to 83.33 trillion won, as operating margins expanded to 80% from 47% in the prior year. EPS jumped as well to 54,454 won per share from 17.850 won per share in the year-ago period.

Crucially, the company expects demand to outpace supply through 2030, as the company secured long-term agreements with 14 major customers, covering more than 50% of its total production capacity for 2027 and 2028.

Meanwhile, cash flow from operating activities rose by 281.3% over the past year to 54.8 trillion as the company closed the quarter with a mammoth cash balance of 114.5 trillion won, much higher than its short-term debt levels of 4.56 trillion won.

Shareholder activities also remained robust as the company returned 14 trillion won as dividends, with plans to return 100 trillion won in FY 2026.

Shifting focus to valuations, SKHY ADR is trading at a discount to its peers. Its forward P/E, P/S, and P/CF of 5.49, 2.84, and 5.94 are all below the sector medians of 29.81, 3.37, and 20.43, respectively.

Analyst Opinion on SKHY Stock

Taking all of this into account, analysts have assigned an overall rating of "Strong Buy" for SKHY stock. The mean target price of $248.82 denotes a potential upside of 52% from current levels. Out of 16 analysts covering the stock, 12 have a "Strong Buy" rating, two have a "Moderate Buy" rating, and two have a "Hold" rating.

news.Title: Is Apple a Top Tech Stock to Buy Now?
news.Content:
Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) has been sneakily delivering a strong 2026. It's up about 27% this year, easily outperforming the market. It's doing it without the fanfare of artificial intelligence (AI), although it has made some improvements in that area.

However, after such a great run in 2026, is it still a solid stock to buy now? I think history says it's not.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Business performance and stock performance are misaligned

Apple's business needs little introduction. Almost everyone in the U.S. has interacted with an Apple product at one time or another, and it has a strong grip on the consumer hardware space. However, this isn't typically considered a high-growth industry. Consumers only have so much money to spend on electronics and other gadgets, and Apple has saturated the market. Whether it's a phone, laptop, or watch, there's an Apple product for that. For years, Apple struggled with slow growth, but it has recently broken out above the 10% year-over-year growth mark.

AAPL Revenue (Quarterly YoY Growth) data by YCharts.

That comes after years of single-digit-to-negative growth, and it has the market excited. However, there are questions as to how long this will last. There's currently a substantial smartphone upgrade cycle underway, and once it wraps up, Apple could have a tough time keeping up with sales.

From a stock perspective, Apple's growth is underperforming its stock performance, which has pushed Apple to some valuation extremes.

Over the past decade, Apple stock breached 40 times earnings twice.

AAPL PE Ratio data by YCharts.

Each time it did so, the valuation declined by 25% to 30 times earnings or lower. That pattern looks slated to repeat itself in 2027 and could make Apple returns a bit scarce next year unless it can grow its way out of it.

However, with Wall Street analysts projecting 10% revenue growth in 2027, it's clear it won't grow substantially faster than the broader market. The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) tends to grow at about a 10% pace on average. If Apple's revenue growth is at the same pace, then having nearly double the price tag doesn't make a ton of sense (the S&P 500 trades for 23.2 times earnings).

As a result, I think there are far better stocks to buy right now than Apple. The pattern is pretty clear that Apple's stock doesn't get much more expensive than this, so there will be far better times to buy in the future.

Story Continues

news.Title: Are Options Traders Betting on a Big Move in MKSI Stock?
news.Content:
Investors in MKS Inc. MKSI need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the Dec. 18, 2026 $170 Call had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

What is Implied Volatility?

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

What do the Analysts Think?

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for MKSI shares, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently, MKSI is a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) in the Electronics - Miscellaneous Products industry that ranks in the Top 19% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 60 days, one analyst has increased the earnings estimates for the current quarter, while none dropped the estimates. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current quarter from $3.63 per share to $3.64 in that period.

Given the way analysts feel about MKSI right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there's a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

news.Title: 'The Fed put is very much back': Wall Street strategists weigh central bank's next move
news.Content:
Wednesday's Fed decision this week to keep interest rates unchanged despite sticky inflation fueled by oil prices above $100 per barrel was a head-scratcher for more than one Wall Street strategist.

"In our view, the decision was puzzling," Ed Yardeni of Yardeni Research wrote last week.

"It reminds us of someone standing in a room with a fire alarm blaring and smoke pouring under the door, yet insisting on more evidence before calling the fire department," he noted, highlighting that the US economy increased at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter.

Others have questioned whether the Fed put — in which the central bank would step in to support financial markets by lowering interest rates or providing liquidity amid declining asset prices — could come into play.

"The Fed put is very much back," Darius Dale, founder of 42 Macro, said on Yahoo Finance on Thursday. Dale expects that, going forward, policy will include greater coordination between the Federal Reserve and the Treasury to influence the bond market, the government's means of issuing debt.

That coordination could include officials eventually stepping in to buy back government bonds using cash backed by the Fed, giving policymakers extra firepower to calm nervous bond markets and provide a liquidity boost next year.

That prospect helps explain why investors have continued to shift between stock market sectors rather than suffer a broader sell-off, despite concerns about inflation, interest rates, and AI jitters.

"This is a market that continues to rotate instead of go down," Dale said. "The market might be looking — eyes on the prize — at a liquidity rescue in 2027."

Indeed, most of the sell-off in recent sessions has happened in tech. Worries over AI funding and the impact of artificial intelligence on businesses such as Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) search software have left certain pockets of the AI trade reeling. Quarterly prints from Intel ( INTC ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) have put pressure on the AI trade.

Meanwhile, Healthcare ( XLV ), Financial Services ( XLF ), and Real Estate ( XLRE ) saw gains last week. Over the past month, every other sector but Technology ( XLK ) and Communications Services ( XLC ) has rallied, according to Yahoo Finance's AlphaSpace data.

"Beneath the hood, the fundamentals of this AI wave still remain really robust," Stephanie Aliaga, global market strategist at JPMorgan Global Asset Management, told Yahoo Finance.

Story Continues

"But we are entering a more discerning phase of this AI trade, and not every company is going to shine as bright, particularly in an environment with higher financing costs," she added.

Aliaga said fixed income is an attractive time to add to portfolios, given bond yields.

UBS strategists also noted that high-quality bonds can help stabilize portfolios, with attractive yields providing investors with income even as bond prices fluctuate.

"We continue to see scope for equity gains overall and believe investors should focus on building a resilient portfolio that includes exposure beyond tech," said Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, chief investment officer of the Americas and global head of equities at UBS.

news.Title: Intel Has a Massive Warning for AMD Stock Investors. Is It Time to Book Profits Before Nov. 3?
news.Content:
Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) released its third-quarter results on Oct. 29, and shares of the company crashed more than 28% the following day.

The primary reason behind the bloodbath in Intel stock was its weaker-than-expected guidance. Though Intel guided for a strong year-over-year increase in both revenue and earnings, Wall Street was expecting more. However, the sharp drop in personal computer (PC) sales this year offset the impressive gains that Intel enjoyed in the data center segment.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

That doesn't bode well for Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD). Let's look at the reasons why.

Image source: Getty Images.

AMD's reliance on the PC market could dent investor confidence in the stock

When AMD released its second-quarter results in August, the company reported a healthy 23% year-over-year increase in revenue from sales of client central processing units (CPUs) for PCs. The segment's revenue landed at $3.1 billion, accounting for 27% of its top line.

Similarly, Intel's revenue from its client computing segment was up by 13% year over year in Q2 to $8.9 billion. However, the script flipped in Q3, with Intel reporting a 5% year-over-year drop in client computing revenue to $8.1 billion. The company blamed poor PC sales for this decline, which isn't surprising as the market has been going through a rough patch due to high memory costs and component shortages.

Counterpoint Research estimates that global PC shipments dropped 21% year over year in Q3. The firm expects Q4 to be even worse, with a 27% drop from the year-ago period. Similarly, Intel noted that the PC decline has accelerated recently amid high costs that are pressuring companies' IT budgets. So, AMD could feel the heat when it releases Q3 results after the market closes on Nov. 3.

Intel also pointed out that PC shipments will drop around 10% in 2027, with "year-over-year declines to be more pronounced during the first half." The situation could improve in the second half of 2027 due to easier comparisons from the year-ago period. However, AMD's client CPU business may face near-term challenges.

Should investors book profits in AMD ahead of its quarterly report?

AMD stock has jumped 90% over the past year, which is why investors may be wondering whether they should take profits off the table. Well, the broader market sentiment on artificial intelligence (AI) stocks suggests that booking profits could be the right move. However, if AMD suffers a steep fall following its Nov. 3 report, it may be a smart idea to buy it for multiple reasons.

Story Continues

First, Intel's PC decline isn't just attributable to the broader market's troubles. Chipzilla has been losing share to AMD in this space. Mercury Research notes that AMD's share of the client CPU market increased by 6.4 percentage points year over year in Q2. So, AMD may not suffer the same decline as Intel did in its PC-focused business last quarter.

Second, Intel noted that the demand for AI-focused chips from data centers is increasing. For instance, Intel expects server CPU unit shipments to increase by 30% this year and next. The good news for AMD is that it is gaining share from Intel in server CPUs as well. AMD's Q2 server CPU share was 34.5%, up from 27.3% a year ago.

So, the growth of AMD's data center business could be much stronger than Intel's, driven by its market share gains and an increase in server CPU prices due to short supply. In all, I won't be surprised to see AMD doing better than Intel when it releases its Q3 results. But if the stock drops following its report, buying it could be a smart move.

After all, AMD's earnings per share (EPS) are anticipated to increase at a 65% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) over the long run, according to YCharts. Also, the stock trades at less than 32 times forward earnings, which isn't all that expensive considering that its EPS growth is anticipated to accelerate from 83% in 2026 to 109% next year.

So, any potential decline in AMD's shares following Intel's quarterly report, as well as its own Q3 earnings on Nov. 3, can be treated as a buying opportunity due to its terrific growth potential and valuation.

news.Title: The AI Red Queen Effect: Why Big Tech Can’t Afford to Stop Spending
news.Content:
There's an interesting situation developing among the biggest technology companies in the world. Nobody wants to be the first to stop spending money on artificial intelligence (AI). It's like a big game of chicken, only with hundreds of billions of dollars at stake.

Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL), and Meta Platforms (META) are investing heavily in data centers, chips, and other AI infrastructure needed to build out AI. They keep opening their checkbooks, even as analysts (and investors) start to question whether that spending will pay off.

More News from Barchart

What to Expect From AMD's Q3 Earnings

SpaceX Reportedly Faces Higher Borrowing Costs on Its $40 Billion GPU Deal. What It Means for SPCX Stock.

How Investors Should View the Launch of Alphabet's Gemini 4 Carbon

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

GF Securities analyst Henry Huang has a name for what's happening—the "AI Red Queen Effect"—in reference to Lewis Carroll's "Through the Looking-Glass," where the Red Queen tells Alice that it takes all the running you can do just to stay in the same place, and if you want to get somewhere, you need to go twice as fast.

For the hyperscalers, that means spending enormous amounts of money simply to keep up with their competitors. And Huang argues that they're more willing to risk spending too much than risk falling behind.

Nobody Wants to Lose the AI Race

The executives running these companies aren't exactly hiding their intentions.

Amazon CEO Andy Jassy made his position clear in April when he defended his company's capex plan. "We're not going to be conservative in how we play this," Jassy wrote in his annual shareholder letter.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has been even more direct. In a September 2025 interview, Zuckerberg acknowledged that an AI bubble was possible. But he said the risk of spending too much was less concerning than missing an opportunity to lead the next generation of technology.

"If we end up misspending a couple of hundred billion dollars, I think that that is going to be very unfortunate, obviously," Zuckerberg said.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella also defended AI infrastructure spending at Morgan Stanley's technology conference in March. Nadella argued that software improvements, better equipment utilization, and a diverse customer base could help Microsoft generate attractive returns on its investments.

Story Continues

Alphabet isn't sitting on the sidelines, either. Google's parent company plans to spend $200 billion this year—double its capex budget in 2025. "The competition in AI infrastructure is the most critical and also the most expensive part of the AI race," Amin Vahdat, Google's infrastructure lead, said in November.

The AI Red Queen Has an Expensive Appetite

Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet operate the world's largest cloud computing businesses. Their customers need access to increasingly powerful AI systems, and those systems require substantial computing capacity.

If Microsoft cannot provide enough capacity, customers could turn to Amazon or Google. The same problem works in reverse.

Meta isn't selling cloud infrastructure on the same scale, but it's investing in AI models and products that could influence the future of its advertising and social media businesses, as well as its Muse AI assistants.

Huang, of GF Securities, projects capital expenditures among the five largest U.S. cloud service providers will grow 85% in 2026, another 53% in 2027, and 20% in 2028.

And while GF Securities expects the hyperscalers to maintain healthy balance sheets, having enough money to keep spending doesn't necessarily mean every investment will generate an attractive return.

What Should Investors Make of the AI Spending Race?

There are already signs that the spending is producing results.

Amazon reported that AWS generated $42.23 billion in second-quarter revenue. And Microsoft has demonstrated that AI services are contributing to the growth of its Azure cloud platform.

But building data centers is expensive, and those facilities must generate enough revenue to justify their construction and operating expenses. AI chips also become outdated as newer, more powerful hardware arrives.

That's why the Red Queen comparison is so interesting. Each company may have a perfectly reasonable argument for increasing its own spending. But if everyone builds capacity faster than customers can use it profitably, some of those investments could disappoint.

The biggest technology companies can afford to participate in this race. Whether shareholders will be happy with the eventual returns is another matter. Investors should remember that the most important number may not be how much these companies spend on AI but how much profit they can generate from all that spending.

news.Title: Here's the Real Winner of the AI Build-Out
news.Content:
With Anthropic's initial public offering (IPO) quickly approaching, many investors are wondering if it could be the best AI stock to buy right now. While I'm not sure how its IPO will go , it could be quite successful.

Still, I think many other companies will be major winners from the AI build-out, but none as surefire as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM). It holds a unique position in the AI arms race. If you're looking for a stock that can grow at an optimized pace, with little chance of failure, Taiwan Semiconductor is your stock.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Anthropic's IPO is filled with second-hand references to Taiwan Semiconductor

Throughout its IPO, Anthropic discusses how it uses multiple types of computing units to increase performance while reducing costs. The industry standard is the Nvidia GPU. These units can be used for nearly all tasks and deliver high performance across nearly every area.

However, specialized computing units can perform better in some situations. Chips like Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) from Alphabet or Trainium chips from Amazon can deliver better performance at a lower price in some applications, but not all. When applicable, Anthropic will divert workloads to these chips, but will always have Nvidia's GPUs to do the rest. In addition to Nvidia's GPUs, it's also starting to source some from Advanced Micro Devices when the outright performance from Nvidia GPUs isn't necessary.

That's a wide range of computing units for one company, but it makes the most sense for Anthropic's structure. However, all these computing units have one thing in common: Most, if not all, of their chips come out of a Taiwan Semiconductor facility. This means that it doesn't really matter which company has the best computing unit at the time; as long as they're buying computing units in general, there's a good chance that Taiwan Semiconductor is getting a cut of the pie.

This makes Taiwan Semiconductor a universal AI stock, as it doesn't care which computing unit is being bought, as long as they're buying. Judging by Anthropic and its peers' AI build-out plans, they will be buying AI chips for a long time.

Taiwan Semiconductor confirmed this on its latest conference call, having previously provided guidance for a 50% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) in AI chips from 2024 to 2029. An analyst asked for an updated figure, and CEO C.C. Wei stated that demand is robust and that it will likely exceed that CAGR. That's impressive guidance, and all TSMC knows is that demand will be massive and elevated.

Story Continues

As a result, I think TSMC is a very smart buy for investors. However, its stock isn't valued at an extreme level, either.

Taiwan Semiconductor is attractively priced

As we approach the end of 2026, valuing the stock based on 2027 earnings estimates becomes a smart idea. Taiwan Semiconductor trades at less than 19 times next year's earnings.

TSM PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts

While that's not a bargain-bin price, it isn't far off the S&P 500 , which trades for 19.2 times forward earnings when the next 12 months are used. So, the market has essentially priced TSMC as a market-average stock, even though we know it will experience market-crushing growth from the AI build-out.

Few companies will benefit more from increased AI usage than Taiwan Semiconductor. With the massive amount of money expected to be spent on AI infrastructure over the next few years, it's a no-brainer investment, and if you don't own shares, it's not too late to buy.

news.Title: MKBHD drops a blunt verdict on Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro
news.Content:
A laptop is a tool you touch all day, just not usually on the screen.

Your hands live on the keyboard and trackpad. The display sits upright, a foot or two away, and that setup has barely changed in decades.

Apple liked it that way. For years, the company argued that reaching up to poke a laptop screen was a bad idea, even as rivals added touchscreens to Windows machines.

That stance made the Mac different from almost every other premium laptop. It also kept Apple's line between the Mac and the iPad clear.

So when Apple finally put touch on a Mac, the obvious question was whether it works. One of the most-watched tech reviewers on YouTube just gave his answer.

Apple (AAPL) announced the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display on Oct. 28, calling it the first Mac with Touch, according to its press release . Pre-orders are open, and the laptops will reach customers and stores on Friday, Nov. 6.

Marques Brownlee, the YouTube reviewer known as MKBHD, tried it in a first-impressions video titled "Macbook PROLED XDR Impressions: They Said They Wouldn't!" His verdict on the headline feature was cool.

"It's still kind of sloppy and messy to use it," Brownlee said, Dexerto reported.

What MKBHD didn't like about the touchscreen Mac

Brownlee laid out his objections plainly. "I never want fingerprints on my display," he said, adding that he also never wants "the display wobbling around as I'm touching it," according to Dexerto .

He also didn't want to "hold my arm out and have my arm get tired."

That's the same complaint Steve Jobs made about vertical touchscreens in 2010. "It doesn't work, it's ergonomically terrible," Jobs said at the time, Gulf News noted.

Here are the main problems Brownlee flagged, according to Dexerto and Gulf News:

The screen still wobbles. Apple stiffened the hinge slightly, but the display still moves when pressed.

No Apple Pencil. The MacBook Pro doesn't support it.

Mac apps aren't built for fingers. Most desktop software still assumes a keyboard and trackpad, and many demos he saw involved mis-touches and fumbles.

Apple adapted the Mac rather than rethinking it. He said Apple is "adapting for you," for example by enlarging small buttons so they're easier to tap.

Tom's Guide Editor-in-Chief Mark Spoonauer raised the same Pencil gap in his own hands-on. "We'll have to see how well touch works with third-party apps," he wrote .

Why MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display costs you $400 more

This is the number I'd focus on. The 14-inch touch model with the M5 Pro chip starts at $2,899, while the existing 14-inch MacBook Pro with the same chip and a mini-LED screen costs $2,499, PPC Land reported.

Story Continues

Apple is keeping the mini-LED models on sale alongside the new ones, MacRumors reported. So the $400 buys the OLED panel, the touch layer, the lighter body and the Dynamic Island, not more computing power.

Related: Apple is about to break a rule Steve Jobs defended

Here's how the lineup stacks up in the U.S., according to Apple and PPC Land:

14-inch MacBook Pro, M6: $1,999

14-inch MacBook Pro, M5 Pro (mini-LED): $2,499

14-inch MacBook Pro, M5 Pro (PROLED XDR, touch): $2,899

16-inch MacBook Pro, M5 Pro (PROLED XDR, touch): $3,399

14-inch MacBook Pro, M5 Max (PROLED XDR, touch): $4,499

16-inch MacBook Pro, M5 Max (PROLED XDR, touch): $4,799

By my math, the touch model costs 16% more than the same-chip mini-LED version. It's $900 more than the M6 MacBook Pro, Apple's cheapest new Pro.

If you split the $2,899 base price over 12 months, that's about $241.58 a month before tax.

Apple's Upgrade lease, run through Klarna, starts at $78.99 a month over 24 months at that price, according to Apple. A lease isn't ownership, though, so read the terms before you sign.

What MKBHD liked about the new MacBook Pro

It wasn't all bad. Brownlee found the touchscreen responsive and smooth, with multi-touch gestures, pinch-to-zoom, and touch window management, Dexerto reported.

He also saw a clear use for iPhone app developers, who can tap a simulated iPhone on screen. And he said he's "fine" with touch as an optional feature, even if he's "personally not interested."

More Apple Devices:

MKBHD drops a blunt verdict on Apple's $1,999 iPhone Duo

Apple's $1,999 iPhone Duo appears to have an app problem

Apple cuts iPhone 18 Pro orders as AI raises the bill

The display and the weight impressed him most. "I'd upgrade for the weight savings before I would for the touchscreen," he said, according to Dexerto.

Apple's numbers back that up. The 14-inch model weighs 3 pounds, half a pound lighter than before, and the 16-inch weighs 4 pounds, according to Apple. The OLED panel hits 2,000 nits of peak brightness with a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.

"PROLED XDR is the world's best laptop display," said Johny Srouji, Apple's chief hardware officer, in the release .

Brownlee also noted that the nano-texture finish feels softer to the touch and that both finishes hide fingerprints well, Gulf News reported.

Who should buy the touchscreen MacBook Pro

Based on Brownlee's take, here's how I'd sort it:

Photo and video pros: The screen is the real upgrade, and touch is a bonus.

iPhone app developers: Touch makes testing apps on a simulated iPhone more natural.

Frequent travelers: The half-pound weight cut matters if you carry it every day.

Everyone else: The $2,499 mini-LED model has the same chip. The $1,999 M6 model may be all the laptop you need.

Microsoft Word, Excel, Zoom, and other apps are getting touch support "later this year," Apple said. If touch is your reason to buy, waiting for those updates costs you nothing.

Should you pre-order before Nov. 6?

If you're on the fence, I'd treat this like any big purchase. Decide what you're paying for, and make sure you'll use it.

Students and teachers can save $150 on the 14-inch model, which drops to $2,749 with education pricing, according to Apple . Trade-in credit can also take a chunk off the price.

Brownlee's verdict is a useful filter.

If you want the best screen on a laptop and a lighter bag, the new MacBook Pro delivers.

If you're paying $400 extra mainly to touch the screen, you may be paying for the part of the Mac that still needs work.

Related: JPMorgan resets Apple stock price target amid iPhone panic
