news.Title: If Taiwan Semi Raises Prices, It Could Be Bad News for Intel Stock. Here’s Why.
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) reported plans to raise prices for its advanced chip-on-wafer-on-substrate (CoWoS) packaging technology could be a warning sign for Intel (INTC), even as it underscores the strength of the artificial intelligence (AI) chip market. Reports suggest TSMC could increase CoWoS pricing by 10% to 20%, as demand from AI accelerators, server CPUs, and custom chips continues to strain advanced-packaging capacity. TSMC has not independently confirmed the reported increase, but Wedbush analyst Matt Bryson said that, if accurate, the pricing move would indicate that CoWoS is once again becoming a supply-chain "pinch point." More importantly for Intel, Bryson believes higher TSMC pricing could suggest the company is facing less competitive pressure from Intel's EMIB-T advanced-packaging technology.

That interpretation is particularly important because Intel has been positioning EMIB-T as an alternative to TSMC's CoWoS and has been seeking to win advanced-packaging business from AI chip customers. If TSMC can raise prices despite Intel offering an alternative, it suggests customers may still be willing to pay a premium for TSMC's technology, capacity, and ecosystem, potentially making it harder for Intel to use pricing and capacity as a competitive advantage.

More News from Barchart

What to Expect From AMD's Q3 Earnings

SpaceX Reportedly Faces Higher Borrowing Costs on Its $40 Billion GPU Deal. What It Means for SPCX Stock.

ASML vs. Applied Materials: One Is Growing Twice as Fast, but I'd Buy The Other Instead

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

About Intel Stock

Intel is a leading technology company specializing in the design, development, manufacture, and marketing of semiconductor products, including microprocessors, chipsets, graphics processing units (GPUs), memory, and related hardware for consumer, enterprise, and industrial markets. Headquartered in Santa Clara, California, Intel remains a key player in data center, PC, and emerging AI and networking segments. Intel's market cap is around $505 billion, reflecting its valuation among the world's largest semiconductor companies.

Intel stock has delivered a remarkable rally in 2026 despite significant volatility along the way. Shares are up about 158.9% year-to-date (YTD) and roughly 130% over the past year, reflecting a dramatic shift in investor sentiment around the company's turnaround, AI opportunity, and foundry ambitions. However, the stock has also experienced sharp pullbacks after reaching a 52-week high of $142.35 on June 30. Intel is currently 33% below that peak, highlighting how much volatility has accompanied the rally.

Story Continues

More recently, however, INTC has regained momentum ahead of its third-quarter earnings report. Shares climbed 4% on Oct. 26, 3.6% on Oct. 27, and another 1.9% on Oct. 28, closing at $95.53. This advance followed an 8% decline on Oct. 22, amid a broader semiconductor and AI-stock sell-off. Nevertheless, Intel's upcoming earnings are particularly important as investors assess whether improving AI and data-center demand, higher CPU pricing, and progress in its foundry strategy can support the next leg of the recovery. Notably, the news that TSMC might be considering raising prices did not appear to impact the stock negatively.

The stock is currently trading at a premium to its sector median at 83.10 times forward earnings.

Q2 Results Exceeded Consensus Estimates

Intel released second-quarter 2026 results on July 23, reporting its strongest quarterly revenue growth in more than 15 years.

Its revenue rose 25% year-over-year (YOY) to $16.1 billion. The increase was primarily driven by Intel Products revenue, which climbed 28% YOY, including a 59% increase in Data Center and AI (DCAI) revenue and a 13% increase in Client Computing and Platform Group (CCPG) revenue. Intel said higher average selling prices, particularly from a richer mix of premium products, were a key contributor.

Profitability also improved substantially. Its non-GAAP gross margin rose to 41.8% from 29.7%, while non-GAAP operating margin increased to 17.2% from negative 3.9%. Intel generated $7.0 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter.

While GAAP results remained distorted by significant charges, on an adjusted basis, Intel swung to non-GAAP net income of $2.2 billion, or $0.42 per share, from a $0.4 billion loss, or $0.10 per share, a year earlier and exceeding guidance.

Intel issued stronger-than-expected guidance for the September quarter. The company expects Q3 revenue of $15.8 billion to $16.8 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $0.38.

Intel also increased its expected 2026 capital spending to about $20 billion, reflecting stronger demand and the need to expand manufacturing capacity. Management said it expects investment to increase meaningfully again in 2027.

In addition, analysts predict EPS to be around $1.05 for fiscal 2026, an improvement of 975% YOY, and to surge again by 39.1% annually to an EPS of $1.46 in fiscal 2027. Also, the consensus EPS estimate of $0.28 for Q3 (about to be reported on Oct. 29 after market close) indicates a 154.6% rise YOY.

What Do Analysts Expect for Intel Stock?

Wedbush analyst Matt Bryson maintained a cautious stance with a "Hold" rating and a $98 price target on Intel on Oct. 27.

On the other hand, New Street Research analyst Pierre Ferragu upgraded Intel from "Neutral" to "Buy" on Oct. 26 and assigned a $125 price target, making it one of the most bullish recent analyst calls on the stock.

INTC has a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating overall. Of the 46 analysts covering the stock, 13 advise a "Strong Buy," one recommends a "Moderate Buy," 31 analysts are on the sidelines, giving it a "Hold" rating, and one suggests a "Strong Sell."

INTC's average analyst price target of $113.90 indicates a 19.2% upside, while the Street-high target price of $200 suggests that the stock could rally 109.4%.

news.Title: Lumentum Jumped on Reports Marvell Is in Late-Stage Talks to Acquire the Company. LITE Stock Is a Buy No Matter What.
news.Content:
Lumentum Holdings (LITE) jumped 15% in after-hours trading on Oct. 28 following reports that Marvell Technology (MRVL) was in advanced talks to buy the company. The rally added to a 329% gain over the past year, leaving the stock well above its 52-week low of $184.20.

Investors have been buying into the demand for the company's lasers and optical components, which help move data through AI data centers.

More News from Barchart

What to Expect From AMD's Q3 Earnings

SpaceX Reportedly Faces Higher Borrowing Costs on Its $40 Billion GPU Deal. What It Means for SPCX Stock.

ASML vs. Applied Materials: One Is Growing Twice as Fast, but I'd Buy The Other Instead

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

But Lumentum Holdings cannot make enough to meet that demand. Its optical components are sold out through early 2029, and CEO Michael Hurlston said it could not meet roughly 70% of demand for certain products through 2027. While the takeover reports lifted Lumentum Holdings, Marvell Technology shares fell sharply.

So, is a deal close, or are investors getting ahead of themselves? Let's find out.

How Close Is Marvell to a Deal?

Marvell Technology is reportedly in advanced talks to buy Lumentum, with an agreement possible as soon as early November. That makes a deal look closer, but it is not a guarantee.

The purchase would build on Marvell Technology's push into AI networking, including its February 2026 acquisition of Celestial AI and its Photonic Fabric technology, which helps connect AI processors. Buying Lumentum Holdings would bring more of the lasers and optical components used in those connections under one roof. The companies have also worked together, demonstrating optical circuit switching technology earlier this year.

Investors have reacted differently to the two stocks. By the Oct. 29 close, Marvell Technology had dropped more than 13%, while Lumentum Holdings finished about 0.6% higher.

For now, the talks remain just that. The report does not establish a signed agreement or confirmed purchase price. Until the companies announce terms, investors still cannot judge what Marvell Technology would pay or what Lumentum Holdings shareholders would receive.

The Business Behind the Buyout Interest

Lumentum Holdings just posted strong fiscal fourth-quarter results. Revenue jumped 109.3% from a year ago to $1.006 billion. Components sales rose 102.7% to $649.4 million, while Systems revenue climbed 122.6% to $356.9 million. Adjusted gross margin improved to 50.4% from 37.8%, and adjusted operating margin hit 36.6% versus 15% last year.

Story Continues

Adjusted EPS came in at $3.23, up from $0.88. A $7.8 billion noncash debt-extinguishment charge did push the company to a $7.16 billion GAAP net loss. Looking ahead, management expects fiscal Q1 2027 revenue between $1.225 billion and $1.275 billion, with adjusted EPS of $4.05 to $4.35. That growth is already showing up in the stock.

The company is also moving closer to the AI chips themselves. On September 21, Lumentum Holdings showed off an optical-connectivity design with Qualcomm (QCOM) and Corning (GLW). The setup pairs Lumentum's lasers with their interface and fiber tech to create faster, lower-power links between AI processors.

In March 2026, the company also bought a 240,000-square-foot manufacturing plant in Greensboro, North Carolina. The site will make indium-phosphide lasers for big AI data centers, and NVIDIA (NVDA) is listed as a key customer there.

What Analysts See Beyond the Takeover

Lumentum Holdings reports its next earnings on November 5 after the market closes. Analysts are looking for September-quarter EPS of $3.82, up 536.67% from $0.60 a year ago. For the full fiscal 2027 year, the estimate is $19.79, a 143.42% jump from $8.13.

Piper Sandler stuck with its "Overweight" rating and $400 target on Marvell Technology, not on Lumentum. The firm pointed out that optical networking helps move AI data faster while using less power. It called Lumentum's high-powered lasers a key enabling technology and noted the two companies already showed complementary optical tech earlier this year. The idea is that putting those pieces together could handle more of the connectivity needs from bigger AI systems.

Before the takeover talk even started, Lumentum got a fresh bullish call. StoneX started coverage on October 26 with a "Buy" rating and a $1,200 price target. Analyst Cody Acree focused on the company's own business outlook. Management now sees demand for near-packaged optics possibly showing up in late 2027 or early 2028, earlier than they thought before. Acree called it "a credible deployment architecture rather than distant optionality" and pointed to continuous-wave lasers, external light-source assemblies, and optical engines as the products that could benefit.

Right now, all 26 analysts covering Lumentum Holdings give it a consensus "Strong Buy" rating. The average price target sits at $1,170.19, which is about 27.26% higher than the current share price levels.

Conclusion

Whether Marvell actually closes a deal for Lumentum is still an open question. The advanced talks and clear strategic fit give the rumor real weight, yet valuation gaps and regulatory hurdles can still kill it. Even without a buyout, Lumentum's sold-out capacity through 2029 and surging optical demand already support the stock's strong run. Shares look more likely to keep grinding higher on fundamentals than to collapse if talks fall apart. The next catalyst is the November 5 earnings report, which should show whether the business itself continues to deliver.

news.Title: ORCL Stock Has a Solid Base to Build on After Q1, Especially as Oracle Announces Key AI Partnerships
news.Content:
A key argument often put forth against Oracle (ORCL) optimists was that the company's thriving cloud business stood on one strong pillar — OpenAI. The recently held Oracle World AI conference went some way to dispel that notion when the company extended partnerships with some of the key players of the AI industry, which included chipmakers and hyperscalers.

Shares are up about 11% since the conclusion of the conference, with Oracle inking deals with the likes of Nvidia (NVDA), OpenAI, Google (GOOG) (GOOGL), Cerebras (CBRS), Snowflake (SNOW), and Intel (INTC). However, shares are still down 28.4% on a YTD basis as the company's market cap stands at $437.1 billion.

More News from Barchart

Dear CoreWeave Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 10

Dear Palantir Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 2

'I Held Out Until It Got Back To Almost Where I Paid For It And Then I Sold It': Late Billionaire Charlie Munger Once Admitted He Made The Classic Amateur Mistake

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

What Went Down At Oracle AI World?

Even though Oracle did forge renewed partnerships with many, the most eye-catching one remained the one with OpenAI. Oracle announced deeper integration of OpenAI models, ChatGPT and Codex across its applications, database and cloud offerings, with announced products including an AI Workspace for accessing Oracle software through ChatGPT, an App Composer for building applications, security capabilities, and a small-business bundle.

Oracle also announced Oracle AI Security Mesh, a managed cybersecurity service that uses OpenAI's advanced cyber models to help identify and remediate vulnerabilities across applications and infrastructure. The offering is designed to work across Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), other cloud platforms and on-premises environments.

Strategically, these could help Oracle earn more from enterprise AI adoption rather than relying primarily on supplying computing capacity. Yet, the counterweight is that OpenAI is already a major infrastructure customer, so deeper integration is not equivalent to diversifying that exposure.

Then, an industry-first phenomenon occurred when the company announced that Google's TPUs would become available on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure in calendar 2027, making OCI the first hyperscale cloud outside Google to offer them, with deployment ramping over several years, as Oracle looks to reduce dependence on Nvidia for chips.

Story Continues

However, the chip leader was a feature at the conference as Oracle also announced expanded Nvidia Vera Rubin supercluster plans and additional offerings involving Cerebras (CBRS) and SambaNova, while Snowflake's data platform was announced as a native Oracle service.

Yet, ORCL stock essentially soared on news related to the company's financial position.

At its Investor Day on October 28, Oracle set a target of more than $225 billion in total revenue by fiscal 2030, alongside a non-GAAP operating margin of at least 40% and non-GAAP earnings per share of more than $21. Management expects revenue to compound at more than 35% annually between FY2026 and FY2030. For context, Oracle generated $67.4 billion in revenue in FY2026, up 17% year over year. The new outlook therefore implies a substantial acceleration in growth, driven by the combination of cloud infrastructure, databases and enterprise applications.

Moreover, Oracle expects free cash flow to turn positive in the second half of FY2028, followed by at least $30 billion in free cash flow in FY2029, while committing to limit additional capital-market funding through FY2030 to $20 billion, excluding refinancing of existing debt, comprising approximately $10 billion in equity and $10 billion in gross debt.

Finally, the company expects its growth to become self-funded from FY2029 and net debt to adjusted EBITDA to fall below 3.5 times that year.

Q1 Can Be a Solid Base to Build Upon

Granted, Oracle's latest results may not have alleviated all concerns around the company. Yet, it can be a start. A very good one at that.

In the first quarter, Oracle delivered record revenue of $19.34 billion, representing a 30% increase from the prior year and surpassing Street estimates by $215.9 million. Total cloud revenue, which now accounts for 60% of overall company revenue compared with 48% a year earlier, reached $11.61 billion, up 62% year over year.

OCI, the company's primary growth focus, more than doubled its revenue to $7.4 billion. Momentum accelerated after management disclosed that it had brought online an additional 850 megawatts of data center capacity while tripling the number of graphics processing units delivered in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 to 300000.

Remaining performance obligations a key measure of future demand, continued to climb, rising 31.5% year over year to $664 billion. This marked the ninth consecutive quarter of RPO growth, and the company expects roughly half of the total to convert into revenue over the next three years.

Earnings per share advanced 30% to $1.92, exceeding the consensus estimate of $1.74. The result represented the fourth straight quarter of earnings beats. Although gross margins declined to 60% from 67% a year earlier, reflecting the costs of expanding data center infrastructure, operating margins held steady at 42%. Capital expenditures increased sharply to $28.5 billion from $8.5 billion in the year-ago period as construction continues at full pace across sites in Texas, New Mexico, Wisconsin, and Michigan.

Net cash from operating activities remained strong at $23.1 billion, up 185.2% year over year. Free cash flow, however, stayed negative at $5.4 billion, widening from $1.9 billion in the prior sequential period. Oracle closed the first quarter with $36.4 billion in cash, well above its short-term debt of $7.6 billion. Total debt nevertheless exceeded $156 billion while interest expense rose 55% from the previous year to $1.4 billion.

The company raised its full-year earnings per share guidance to $8.10 from the $8.05 outlook provided earlier in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Total revenue guidance of $90 billion was left unchanged.

For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Oracle expects revenue growth of 30% to 34% year over year and earnings per share between $1.85 and $1.93, with the midpoint aligning with the consensus estimate of $1.89.

The subdued performance of the stock this year has brought Oracle's valuation to attractive levels. The forward price-to-earnings ratio of 18.46 times and price-to-cash-flow multiple of 7.71 times both sit below the respective sector medians of 22.46 times and 19.75 times. The forward price-to-sales ratio of 5.02 times stands only modestly above the sector median of 3.37 times.

Analyst Opinion

Thus, analysts have deemed ORCL stock to be a "Strong Buy" with a mean target price of $240.66, which denotes a potential upside of 72.4% from current levels. Out of 43 analysts covering the stock, 31 have a "Strong Buy" rating, one has a "Moderate Buy" rating, 10 have a "Hold" rating, and one has a "Strong Sell" rating.

news.Title: Reddit stock plunges 29.2% as Google AI cuts US traffic
news.Content: Updated to reflect Reddit closing stock price on 10/30/2026 Reddit's stock plunged 29.2% on Friday, October 30, after the company said its U.S. audience is shrinking due to Google's AI search features. The sell-off came even though third-quarter revenue jumped 53% to $895 million . U.S. daily users fell to 50.7 million, down 2.5 million from the prior quarter, and CEO Steve Huffman said search referrals dropped by more than 1 million a week in October. Shares, which closed at $129.60 on October 29, traded below their 52-week low of $119.27, changing hands at $91.73 at 4 pm EDT. For investors who bought Reddit as an AI winner, the message is that the same technology is now taking away the traffic that feeds the business. Reddit is tied deeply to Google Reddit runs the discussion forums where users post questions, advice and opinions, and it makes money mainly from advertising. Much of its audience arrives from Google searches, which is why search changes matter so much. The stock has been popular with retail investors, but its data is also valuable to AI companies. In 2024, Reddit inked deals with Google and OpenAI , allowing their respective Gemini and ChatGPT large language models to train on Reddit content in exchange for $60 million and $70 million per year, respectively. Related: Googling for Reddit answers is about to get harder Deals like that have supported revenue, but concern is that AI overviews are reducing traffic to Reddit by more than the company is pocketing from its AI deals. Reddit reports "daily active uniques," or DAUq, split between logged-in users, who tend to be more engaged, and logged-out users, who often arrive from search and see fewer ads and less engagement. That split is the heart of today's drop. In Q3, global DAUq rose 12% year-over-year to 130.3 million. However, U.S. DAUq fell 1% year-over-year, as a 4% dip in logged-out users overwhelmed a 1% increase in logged-in users. "Google has really shifted in their relationship with the rest of the Internet," said CEO Steve Huffman on Reddit's earnings call . "People still want Reddit. It's just Google is not sending them to Reddit the way they used to." Reddit quarter was far from a disaster, but worries remain Reddit revenue in the third quarter rose a more than healthy 53% to $895 million and while DAUq saw headwinds, U.S. revenue was still up 50% to $719 million. As a result, Reddit's profit improved, with diluted EPS clocking in at $1.40, above Wall Street estimates of $1.33. More Artificial Intelligence: Story Continues AI's biggest business opportunity may not look like AI AI racks are outgrowing old power: 2 chipmakers have a strategy BofA splits software into winners and losers as AI agents arrive Those are healthy figures, but the worry over DAUq trumped them, particularly because user engagement fell sequentially. U.S. daily users fell 4.7% from the second quarter, and again, logged-out users were to blame, given they slipped 9%. Management didn't offer a convincing outlook that things would improve, either, given guidance for the fourth quarter was for revenue between $1 billion and $1.03 billion, below analysts' $1.045 billion consensus outlook. "The reality is the AI Mode does not drive traffic, not for us and not to anybody as far as I know," said Huffman. "It used to be a traffic driver. Now it's not." Q4 daily users could fall by a "low double-digit percentage" if Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode trends continue. Wall Street issues a glum verdict on Reddit stock JP Morgan cut its Reddit stock price target to $150 from $185, citing search traffic headwinds, according to TheFly. com . Similar verdicts were issued by other analysts, including Goldman Sachs, which lowered its Reddit price target to $140 from $215 because of weaker search referrals and declines in traffic from logged-out users. Reddit isn't ignoring the logged-out user drop, but COO Jen Wong did point out that 80% of monetization comes from logged-in and app users, making them more important. From here, the key will be whether U.S. logged-in users hold above 23.4 million and whether Q4 revenue lands at or above $1.0B, the low end of guidance, when Reddit reports early next year. Also watch Google's AI search rollout, as it could continue to soften Reddit traffic, and Reddit's tests of logged-in-only access — a move it hopes can shore up its user base. news.Title: Alphabet's Earnings Horror Show Continues, But GOOG Stock Is a Buy Below $300
news.Content:
Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL) released its Q3 earnings on Oct. 28, after markets closed. The search giant's earnings missed on most metrics and dampened the already tepid sentiment towards the stock. GOOG is trading sharply lower today, reminiscent of the crash after its Q2 earnings.

Following today's crash, Alphabet has turned negative for the year and further expanded its underperformance versus its average Magnificent 7 peer. It is quite a reversal of fortunes for GOOG, which was the best-performing Mag 7 stock last year with 65% gains.

More News from Barchart

Dear CoreWeave Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 10

Dear Palantir Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 2

'I Held Out Until It Got Back To Almost Where I Paid For It And Then I Sold It': Late Billionaire Charlie Munger Once Admitted He Made The Classic Amateur Mistake

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

After being bearish on Alphabet for much of this year, mainly on valuation and soaring artificial intelligence (AI) capex, I noted that the stock was well set up heading into Q3 earnings. However, the earnings were disappointing and were far worse than the previous report, where at least the stellar beat on cloud revenues was a major positive.

Alphabet Missed on Most Metrics in Q3

This time around, Alphabet missed on both the top line and the bottom line, and while cloud revenues doubled in the quarter, they were largely in line with estimates. If anything, they fell short of some of the optimistic estimates. Just as with Nvidia (NVDA), the bar is not the "consensus" but the Street-high estimate when it comes to Google's cloud business. The company failed to clear that bar, which added fuel to the sell-off.

Alphabet's Search revenues also decelerated in Q3 when compared with the previous quarter. There were headwinds from adverse forex movements and some ad budgets getting drawn to Q2 due to the FIFA World Cup, but lower monetization in AI mode is also to blame. While Alphabet is scaling ads in AI overviews and AI mode, for now the monetization is below what it generates in traditional search.

Alphabet Warns of 'Significant' Increase in 2027 Capex

During my pre-earnings analysis, I noted that Alphabet needs to calm nerves over its AI capex. The company maintained its 2026 capex budget but warned of a "significant" increase next year, reserving more details for the next earnings call.

Story Continues

The AI buildout is taking a toll on Alphabet's free cash flows, and it reported negative free cash flows of $9.1 billion in Q3, marking its second consecutive quarter of cash burn. The company warned that its growing capex "will put pressure on free cash flows," signalling more quarters of cash burn.

While CFO Anat Ashkenazi said that Alphabet is uniquely positioned "to be able to monetize our AI investments across many products that reach billions of users and enterprises," markets have stopped buying that often repeated story of AI driving long-term growth and are looking for signs of current monetization along with a timeline for positive free cash flows.

Alphabet's commentary on capex and free cash flows failed to calm nerves. As I noted previously, one of the reasons Microsoft (MSFT) has soared from its 2026 lows is because the company forecasted positive free cash flows next year despite the increase in capex. Markets want to hear something similar from other tech giants, especially as rising interest rates make the AI buildout even more costly.

GOOG Stock Looks a Buy Below $300

I previously booked profits when Alphabet stock soared past $400. The stock had run ahead of fundamentals at its peak, and its valuations appeared stretched. However, as Alphabet stock falls below $300, I believe it looks like an attractive "buy" despite all the concerns discussed above.

Consensus estimates call for Alphabet to report earnings per share (EPS) of around $15 next year. At a stock price of $300, it gives us a 2027 price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 20x, which is quite decent. The company has several growth drivers for 2027 and beyond, including its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), whose third-party sales are expected to increase significantly next year.

There are macro risks from a slowing global economy amid high inflation taking a toll on ad spending and lower monetization in AI overviews, coupled with rising search competition from other AI companies impacting Alphabet's core Search business. However, I believe the risks seem more than baked into prices, and I am increasing my GOOG holdings following the crash.

news.Title: Reddit Sinks as Google's AI Shift Takes a Bite Out of Search Traffic. What's Next for RDDT Stock.
news.Content:
Reddit (RDDT) shares slipped sharply on Friday after the company reported a market-beating Q3, but its disappointing revenue guidance and accelerating decline in Google referral traffic spooked investors.

The earnings release led Citizens to downgrade RDDT stock to "Market Perform," highlighting a difficult question for shareholders: Can Reddit expand its advertising business as artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled search answers queries without sending users to the platform?

More News from Barchart

Dear CoreWeave Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 10

Dear Palantir Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 2

'I Held Out Until It Got Back To Almost Where I Paid For It And Then I Sold It': Late Billionaire Charlie Munger Once Admitted He Made The Classic Amateur Mistake

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

Including the post-earnings weakness, Reddit stock is down more than 60% versus the start of this year.

Google's AI Shift Threatens Reddit's Growth Engine

Reddit saw its U.S. daily active unique users decline by about 5% in Q3 compared to Q2, while management warned of a lower-double-digit percentage decline in the fourth.

Google search referrals are falling by more than 1 million per week, according to Citizens' data, threatening the flow of visitors who could eventually become regular, logged-in users. Analyst Andrew Boone also told clients that Google continues to crawl the platform rather heavily, but its AI Overviews and AI mode are sending fewer people back to the site.

The financial implications could emerge gradually. Advertising revenue still came in up 54% year-over-year at $847 million, demonstrating strong monetization. Sustaining that momentum, however, may become more challenging if audience losses persist and Reddit must spend more to attract replacement users.

Citizens Sees Reddit Stock as Fairly Valued

In his research note, Boone said the uncertainty surrounding user growth leaves the Reddit shares fairly valued.

In Q3, the firm's U.S. logged-out daily active uniques came in down 4% compared to last year — their first annual decline since 2022.

Citizens' concern is that weaker traffic increases pressure to extract more revenue from existing users. Higher acquisition spending in 2027 could weigh on profitability, while traffic damage could complicate data-licensing renewals.

Logged-in and app users already account for more than 80% of monetization. Any potential hit on that front, therefore, stands to weigh on RDDT's business and its share price over time.

Story Continues

Wall Street's Consensus View on RDDT Shares

Heading into Oct. 30, Wall Street had a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating on RDDT stock with a mean price target of about $210. However, it's reasonable to expect downward revisions as analysts bake in the company's revenue guidance into their estimates.

news.Title: Can Microsoft Turn a Leaner Workforce and Record AI Spending Into Bigger Profits?
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Microsoft Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

Microsoft offered a voluntary exit package to about 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its workforce, despite strong financial results.

Bulls see the buyouts as a sign of strength, citing 19% revenue growth, 48% Azure growth, and rising Copilot usage offsetting slower headcount.

Bears point to free cash flow falling 27% amid surging AI capital spending, softer Windows revenue, and warnings of potential overcapacity.

Microsoft Corp (NASDAQ: MSFT), the software and cloud giant, has offered a voluntary exit package to around 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its global workforce, in its boldest signal yet that it believes AI can run the business with far fewer people. When a company this profitable opens the door to that many staff at once, it's worth asking what it knows.

The shares, trading near $525 following the company's fiscal year 2027 Q1 results on Oct. 28, gave back their initial post-earnings gains. However, they're still up roughly 10% in 2026 and about 50% above their June 2026 low. In other words, Microsoft isn't offering buyouts because its business is shrinking; it's doing so from a position of financial strength.

→ GE Vernova's Reservations Are Turning Into Real Orders—But the Market Still Wants More.

That's the heart of the debate for investors. Does a leaner headcount point to fatter margins as AI does more of the work, or could substantial departures hint at trouble brewing beneath the AI boom?

The Bull Case: Microsoft Can Afford to Get Leaner

The bullish reading is that Microsoft could be shedding payroll from a position of strength, not because it's scrambling to plug a hole. Revenue in the most recent quarter rose almost 19% to more than $92 billion, operating income landed near $46 billion, and the operating margin held at roughly 50%, a touch higher than a year earlier. Operating expenses rose just 6%, far more slowly than that 19% jump in sales, and headcount had already edged down about 2% year over year as of June 2026, before this latest effort even landed.

→ Phillips 66 Posts Strong Earnings But the Stock Doesn't Care

Layer the AI story on top, and the logic sharpens. Microsoft's Azure platform grew revenue 48% last quarter, daily Copilot users jumped nearly 50% from the prior three months, and management says it's wringing far more work out of the same computing power.

If AI really does let Microsoft generate more revenue per employee, a leaner workforce paired with disciplined spending is exactly how margins could climb from here. Seen that way, the buyout offer is less a cost cut than a reallocation: dollars moving out of payroll and into the data centers Microsoft is betting its next decade on.

Story Continues

→ FTC Puts A Wrinkle In the Cintas and UniFirst Merger

The Bear Case: AI Spending Is Squeezing Cash Flow

The bearish reading starts with that same buildout. Microsoft spent roughly $45 billion on capital projects in a single quarter, expects to clear $50 billion in the next fiscal quarter, and has pointed to something near $170 billion for the calendar year. That's a vast sum to commit before the AI revenue fully shows up, and it's already biting: free cash flow fell 27% to $18.6 billion in the latest quarter as cash capital spending more than doubled. If infrastructure, depreciation, and energy costs outrun the money AI brings in, no amount of payroll trimming will paper over the gap.

There are softer spots, too. Windows OEM and Devices revenue fell 22% in the most recent quarter, and the exit offer reportedly reached even some AI and Copilot teams, which could be seen less as surgical cutting and more as a broad sweep for savings. In addition, Microsoft's 2026 annual report warns, in plain terms, that demand for all this AI capacity could be overestimated and could leave much of its infrastructure underused.

What the Buyouts Could Mean for Microsoft's AI Strategy

Strip it back, and the push for voluntary exits is a statement of intent. Offering buyouts to more than a quarter of staff while pouring record sums into compute raises questions about whether Microsoft expects AI-driven productivity gains to change its long-term staffing needs. However, the company has said AI is not directly driving the buyout program, instead pointing to changing business priorities and workforce needs.

The catch is timing. Microsoft is committing to the costs now and trusting the benefits to arrive later. The tests from here are familiar ones: whether Azure holds its current pace, whether Copilot usage hardens into durable revenue, and whether all that spending earns an acceptable return before investors run short of patience.

Wall Street Still Sees Upside in Microsoft Stock

For now, at least, the analysts are happy to keep leaning into the upside potential. Following the Oct. 28 earnings report, several firms raised their price targets, including Morgan Stanley to $650 and Bank of America to $630. Evercore ISI and J.P. Morgan also maintained bullish ratings, with price targets of $635 and $625, respectively.

They keep pointing to the engine behind the buyout logic: accelerating Azure growth, a massive contracted backlog, and full-stack AI monetization that's turning Copilot and cloud usage into real revenue, all while Microsoft still throws off healthy free cash flow.

That's the bull case in a sentence: the AI spending is being matched by AI income. If that holds, a leaner, heavier-investing Microsoft looks like a company spending from strength. The risk never quite leaves; the returns still have to keep pace with the capital expenditure, but for now, the bullish case has plenty of support.

news.Title: Wall Street's favorite stocks are in their worst slump since 2010: Chart of the Day
news.Content:
Wall Street analysts spent 2026 piling Buy ratings onto the AI build-out. The stocks they ignored have done better.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) stocks with the biggest share of analyst Buy ratings have trailed those with the smallest share for most of the year, according to Piper Sandler chief investment strategist Michael Kantrowitz. Measured year over year, it's the third-worst stretch in Piper's data going back to 1995.

"The Sell Side's MOST favored stocks have underperformed their LEAST favored stocks for the majority of 2026," Kantrowitz wrote in a note to clients Wednesday.

This week showed what that looks like. Alphabet had its worst month in history , Intel had its worst day since 1974 , and the Nasdaq ( ^IXIC ) suffered its biggest daily drop since June as Big Tech's results revived worries about AI spending.

Add it up, and the AI trade has lost about $5 trillion in market value since Oct. 6, by Yahoo Finance calculations, including about $1.6 trillion on Friday alone. Nvidia and Alphabet, two of Piper's favorites, shed about $835 billion each, roughly a third of the total.

The rest of the market has held up. The other 625 large US stocks in Yahoo Finance's count gained about $1.3 trillion over the same stretch, led by Eli Lilly ( LLY ), Walmart ( WMT ) and Exxon Mobil ( XOM ). It's the slump in Wall Street's favorites, playing out in a single month.

Piper picks both groups from the top and bottom of each of the index's 11 sectors, so this isn't tech against everything else.

Only two slumps ran deeper, in 2001-02 and 2010. Both came near big turning points in the market, the first as the tech bubble deflated and the second as stocks recovered from the financial crisis.

Why this hits more portfolios than you'd think

Most investors own Wall Street's favorites whether they picked them or not. Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ) are among the biggest weights in the S&P 500, so any index fund or 401(k) that tracks it leans on their fortunes.

The slump also shows how a crowded idea can work against investors. When nearly every analyst already loves a stock, much of the good news is in the price, and there are few new buyers left to win over. A disappointment then stings.

That's what the favorites are running into. Six of the nine names on Piper's list are down this year, from Alphabet and power producer Vistra ( VST ) to Wynn Resorts ( WYNN ) and Take-Two Interactive ( TTWO ). The exceptions are three AI build-out names: Nvidia, Arista Networks ( ANET ), and Comfort Systems ( FIX ).

Meanwhile, nearly all of the least-loved stocks are up, led by steady names like Kenvue ( KVUE ) and Illinois Tool Works ( ITW ). As a group, though, they've only roughly kept pace with the S&P 500. This is less about the laggards running than about the favorites falling.

Story Continues

A rough week for the AI trade

It looked very different in the spring, when Piper's favorites were up nearly 18% on average, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Then the AI trade began to unwind. It crushed the companies leading the data center build-out first, and this week it reached the megacaps.

That included the biggest one-day drop in market value in Alphabet's history on Thursday, after its third quarter results. Amazon ( AMZN ) and Intel ( INTC ) led tech lower Friday after their own reports, as Amazon's AI build-out pushed its cash burn to a record .

"The AI beta-bubble appears to have already burst!" Kantrowitz wrote. He means the most volatile AI stocks, those with a high beta , which swing more than the market.

That doesn't mean the AI trade is over. Kantrowitz expects investors to move toward beaten-down AI companies with stronger businesses as earnings growth slows. In other words, they're getting pickier about which part of AI they pay for.

"We do not expect a return to an AI-driven market led by the most speculative (i.e., lower quality) stocks," Kantrowitz wrote.

news.Title: How Investors Should View the Launch of Alphabet's Gemini 4 Carbon
news.Content:
Alphabet (GOOGL) shareholders had two major developments to weigh on Oct. 28. Shares of the company finished the regular trading day up by 1.3% after Google unveiled Gemini 4 Carbon, its newest frontier artificial intelligence (AI) model. After the closing bell, however, third-quarter results took center stage and pushed GOOGL stock lower in after-hours trading. The stock fell 13% the next day, Oct. 29, as well as more than 1% on Oct. 30.

Revenue rose about 25% year-over-year (YOY) to $127.6 billion in Q3, with Google Cloud delivering a 103% YOY jump to $30.7 billion. Still, revenue fell slightly short of Wall Street's expectations, while net income also declined. With another model arriving so soon after the release of Gemini 4 Argon in September, Google has more to prove than whether Carbon is technically better.

More News from Barchart

Dear CoreWeave Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 10

Dear Palantir Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 2

'I Held Out Until It Got Back To Almost Where I Paid For It And Then I Sold It': Late Billionaire Charlie Munger Once Admitted He Made The Classic Amateur Mistake

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

Can the latest model help win customers and deliver stronger returns, giving investors another reason to own Alphabet stock? Let's find out.

How Alphabet's Business Is Holding Up

Based in Mountain View, California, Alphabet operates Google Search, YouTube, cloud computing services, and the Gemini AI platform. With a market capitalization of approximately $3.47 trillion, the company's businesses connect advertising customers, enterprise technology buyers, and consumers across products that offer potential distribution channels for new models such as Carbon.

Alphabet stock is now down 11% year-to-date (YTD), and less than 1% for the past 52 weeks. Shares closed at $279.84 on Oct. 30.

GOOGL stock's valuation multiples of 16.9 times trailing earnings and 9.8 times sales exceed sector medians of about 14.2 times and 1.1 times. That places greater pressure on continued growth.

Alphabet released Q3 results on Oct. 28, reporting revenue of $127.6 billion, up 25% YOY but lower than the $127.9 billion expected by analysts. The company's GAAP earnings reached $2.12 per share against consensus estimates of $3.01 — a nearly 30% shortfall — with net income totaling $26.2 billion.

That miss partly reflected an $8.7 billion equity-securities loss versus a $10.7 billion gain a year earlier, separating investment fluctuations from operating performance. Advertising commissions reduced reported revenue to $111.2 billion, below the $111.8 billion analyst forecast.

Story Continues

Google's recent quantum breakthrough offers a useful distinction. Its Willow processor reportedly reduced errors by 40-fold in specially prepared quantum states, but commercially useful systems remain years away.

Meanwhile, management reported 1 billion Gemini app users as of Q3 and anticipates significantly higher 2027 capital expenditures, with details promised during the Q4 earnings call.

Inside Google's Gemini 4 Carbon Launch

Google introduced Gemini 4 Carbon on Oct. 28, positioning its latest frontier model around software engineering and cybersecurity. Beyond generating code, Carbon is designed to handle extended, multistep assignments, including tracing bugs through large software systems and producing fixes. Google says its internal teams have seen the model work for days on complex engineering tasks.

The reported improvements give shareholders something concrete to assess. Carbon scored 59 to lead the updated Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, while Google's internal testing showed more than twice Argon's success rate at generating secure code. These results suggest potential value for enterprise customers, although benchmark performance does not establish commercial demand.

Availability is the immediate constraint. Google is initially granting access to selected cybersecurity defenders through its Fairwind Program while gathering feedback and refining safeguards. Broader access for developers, businesses, and consumers has no firm announced date. Introductory pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, but pricing will double after the introductory period.

The launch therefore represents progress toward potentially valuable paid workloads, not an established earnings driver. Better coding and security tools could encourage adoption, but the investment case still needs evidence of customer usage, revenue contribution, and profitable delivery at scale.

What Do Analysts Expect From Alphabet?

Wall Street expects Alphabet's earnings to keep growing, with average earnings of $3.21 per share expected for the quarter ending December 2026, up from $2.82 a year earlier. That translates into projected growth of 14% YOY.

Alphabet stock has a consensus "Strong Buy" rating across 53 analysts with coverage. The average price target of $410.04 implies potential upside of approximately 47% from current levels. Those expectations give the Carbon launch a financial benchmark.

Conclusion

Gemini 4 Carbon gives Alphabet another way to win business, but it isn't a reason to rush into GOOGL stock. Google still needs to turn better technology into paying customers and a stronger cash flow. The outlook leans bullish over the next year, provided earnings keep growing and heavy spending delivers better returns. Alphabet shares could move higher as results emerge, though the launch alone is unlikely to sustain a rally. Carbon strengthens the story, but customer adoption and financial performance will decide whether shareholders have more to celebrate from here.

news.Title: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy makes a strong prediction on Amazon stock
news.Content:
Amazon just gave Wall Street a quarter it didn't love and a prediction it can't ignore.

Shares slid after the company's third-quarter report, but CEO Andy Jassy used the moment to float a goal no company has ever reached.

"There has never been a trillion dollar revenue business, and we may have two of them in the next 5-10 years," Jassy said in the earnings release .

It's a bold claim, and it puts the spotlight back on what the company's giant spending spree is actually buying.

Amazon's solid quarter still disappointed

On paper, the results looked healthy. Amazon's net sales rose 12% to $201.9 billion, and operating income jumped to $28.1 billion from $17.4 billion a year earlier, good for a 13.9% operating margin that the company called its highest ever, according to Amazon .

Moving Prime Day into the second quarter cut about four percentage points off third-quarter growth.

Also read: Billionaire Bill Ackman doubles down on these stocks in Q2

Investors focused on the misses instead. Revenue came in just shy of the roughly $202.3 billion analysts expected, and earnings of $1.89 a share fell short of the $1.96 forecast. The stock fell about 6% in overnight trading on Oct. 29, even though advertising revenue reached $19.6 billion.

The bigger worry was cash. Amazon's free cash flow over the past 12 months swung to an outflow of $42.4 billion, compared with a $14.8 billion inflow a year earlier, and the company blamed heavier spending on AI infrastructure, Amazon reported .

It still expects about $220 billion in cash capital spending this year. For the fourth quarter, Amazon guided for net sales of $240 billion to $247 billion and operating income of $28.5 billion to $33.5 billion.

The capex number has been climbing all year. Amazon first planned about $200 billion in 2026 capital spending back in February, well above what Wall Street expected, and the stock fell more than 10% on the news. Investors have been asking ever since when all that spending will pay off.

The road to $1 trillion in e-commerce

Jassy's two candidates are Amazon's online stores and its cloud unit, Amazon Web Services. Retail is the much bigger of the two today, and it has the shorter path.

Amazon's North America and International segments, which make up the e-commerce business, brought in $638.3 billion over the past four quarters, and that business has been growing at a low-teens rate in recent years, according to The Motley Fool . At a 10% annual growth rate, that business would top $1 trillion in under five years.

Story Continues

This quarter, though, retail looked sluggish. North America sales rose just 6% to $112.9 billion, and International sales climbed 5% to $43.1 billion, or 8% once you strip out currency moves. Part of that is a calendar quirk: Prime Day landed in the second quarter this year instead of the third.

The retail side was stronger earlier in the year. In the first quarter, North America revenue rose 12% and International jumped 19%, and Bank of America pointed to improving retail as one reason to stay bullish, as reported by TheStreet .

Still, BofA warned that a shift toward essentials and groceries could pressure margins, and it expected free cash flow to stay negative through 2027.

AWS is the harder climb, and the bigger bet

AWS has a much longer road ahead. Its sales rose 39% to $46 billion in the third quarter, putting it at a $184 billion annualized run rate, Forbes reported .

That's impressive growth, but the unit would still need to get roughly five or six times bigger to reach $1 trillion. Wedbush analyst Dan Ives called Jassy's long-term growth outlook "a stronger answer than the quarter alone."

Jassy thinks it can get there. He said AWS "can grow north of 40 percent in each 2027 and in 2028," pointing to "the amount of capacity that we're adding each year." He also said Amazon expects to "spend meaningfully more in 2027," with most of this year's capital budget going to AWS.

Some analysts are even more upbeat. Morgan Stanley's Brian Nowak, who named Amazon a top pick with a $350 price target, expects AWS to grow 47% in 2027 and 42% in 2028, according to TheStreet .

That would nearly triple AWS revenue from 2025 to 2028. Nowak also expects Bedrock, AWS's managed AI service, to become a growing source of high-margin revenue.

More Amazon:

Amazon is coming for your quick Walmart run

Amazon's Alexa shopping tool faces its first big October test

Amazon pulls a best-selling pain reliever again, and customers need to check their medicine cabinets

Demand doesn't seem to be the problem. Back in July, Jassy said that even at its higher spending level, "we will still not have enough capacity to meet all the demand we have in 2026," and AWS's backlog had reached $496 billion.

The question is how fast Amazon can build.

What it means for Amazon investors

The post-earnings drop may have made the stock more interesting. After the sell-off, Amazon was set to trade at roughly 20 times operating income, a far cry from the premium it carried for years, according to The Motley Fool . It's still the world's largest company by revenue, and it's still growing at double-digit rates.

Then there's the money going out the door. Amazon's free cash flow shrank to about $11.2 billion last year from $38.2 billion in 2024, and its debt load has grown substantially as capital spending accelerated.

Jassy has already said spending will go up again in 2027. JPMorgan sees it as a timing issue, since the data centers are built well before the revenue shows up.

For patient investors, Jassy's prediction is the real story. Amazon leads in both online retail and cloud computing, and if AWS keeps growing near the pace Jassy expects, the company could have two trillion-dollar businesses within a decade. Getting there will take a lot of money first.

Related: Morgan Stanley just made a bold call on Amazon stock

Release Date: October 27, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

United Parcel Service Inc ( NYSE:UPS ) exceeded Q3 2026 expectations with consolidated revenue of $22.9 billion, up 6.7% year-over-year, driven by growth across all three segments.

US Domestic segment delivered second consecutive quarter of strong operating profit growth, up over 14% year-over-year, with operating margin expansion of 60 basis points.

International segment returned to year-over-year operating profit growth for the first time since 2025 US trade policy changes, with operating margin of 14.9%.

Supply Chain Solutions revenue grew 17.5% in forwarding and 17.2% in logistics, driven by demand from high-tech, healthcare, manufacturing, and automotive customers.

United Parcel Service Inc ( NYSE:UPS ) raised full-year 2026 outlook, expecting consolidated revenue of approximately $92.6 billion and operating profit of approximately $8.75 billion, with free cash flow of about $6.1 billion.

Negative Points

Total US average daily volume declined 3.3% year-over-year, reflecting deliberate reduction of Amazon volume, with B2B volumes also down year-over-year.

International average daily volume declined 8.7% year-over-year due to geopolitical tensions, though trends improved as the quarter progressed.

Supply Chain Solutions operating profit was $274 million, but Q3 2025 included a $330 million gain from a sale-leaseback transaction, making year-over-year comparison less favorable.

United Parcel Service Inc ( NYSE:UPS ) incurred a net charge of $279 million in Q3 2026, including transformation costs and a goodwill impairment in Supply Chain Solutions.

Fourth quarter US average daily volume is expected to be lower year-over-year due to Amazon volume reduction, and the company will face negative volume comparisons through the first half of 2027.

Q & A Highlights

Q : With the Driver Choice program costs rolling off, how should investors think about free cash flow growth in 2027 and dividend coverage? A : CFO Brian Dykes explained that the elimination of the Driver Choice cash requirement will drive free cash flow improvement next year, though this may be partially offset by how the company funds its pension (referencing the $450 million bond contribution). He emphasized that improving US Domestic margins is the fundamental driver, and as structural changes take hold, free cash flow is expected to rise, improving dividend coverage. CEO Carol Tome added, "Our dividend is safe and secure." Dykes noted the Driver Choice spend was $4 billion this year.

Q : Can you break out the volume trends in the B2B segment and discuss the competitive environment, particularly regarding Amazon's recent push? A : CEO Carol Tome noted that while overall B2B volumes were down year-over-year, 60% of the decline was Amazon-related, leaving underlying performance solid. Regarding competition, she described the pricing environment as "rational" among all competitors. She stated that UPS has not seen any measurable impact from Amazon's shipping announcement this summer, citing differences in network structures (linear vs. reverse logistics) and service guarantees. CFO Brian Dykes added that the Digital Access Program (DAP) is a key driver for premium B2B and air volume mix.

Q : What is the long-term growth algorithm for UPS now that the Amazon volume glide-down is complete? A : CEO Carol Tome outlined a massive addressable market of $922 billion globally, with a $535 billion premium opportunity. The strategy focuses on growing volume and ensuring Revenue Per Piece (RPP) grows faster than Cost Per Piece (CPP) to expand margins. She highlighted specific growth areas, including a $15 billion logistics opportunity associated with data centers and a 30% year-over-year growth in high-tech small package volume. She noted the new global operating model will further enhance network efficiency to drive earnings.

Q : Can you provide more color on the expected margin improvement trajectory for the US Domestic segment? A : CFO Brian Dykes stated that the company expects steady, consistent margin improvement rather than step changes. He pointed to a structural shift in the volume base, with core volume (excluding Amazon) growing nearly 2%, providing better revenue quality. He expects a 50 to 100 basis points spread between RPP and CPP to drive this improvement. CEO Carol Tome added that while margins won't jump from 7.5% to 10% in a single year, the company is committed to improving margins annually by leaning into premium opportunities and productivity.

Q : How much visibility do you have into SMB and Enterprise volume growth continuing into next year, and what are the components of the RPP/CPP spread? A : CEO Carol Tome cited dramatic improvements in churn reduction and a resilient consumer as reasons for confidence in volume visibility. CFO Brian Dykes explained that while the mix benefit from reducing Amazon volume will normalize, the company still expects 200 to 300 basis points of base rate pricing and mix benefit. He noted a constructive pricing environment and the announcement of their General Rate Increase (GRI) consistent with prior years.

Q : When do you expect total volumes to turn positive, and what is driving the step-up in International margins? A : CFO Brian Dykes noted that the company will lap the Amazon volume declines by the second half of next year, but emphasized focusing on core volume growth, which was nearly 2% in Q3. Regarding International, he attributed the Q4 margin step-up (expected ~20%) to peak season demand surcharges and a surge in volume. CEO Carol Tome added that volume trends have improved monthly since the elimination of the de minimis exemption in Europe, with growth in profitable trade lanes like China-US and Asia-to-Asia.

Q : What are the key drivers for the high-value verticals like Healthcare and Data Centers over the next several years? A : CEO Carol Tome identified complex healthcare logistics as a 6% annual growth opportunity and noted the massive potential in data centers, which require complex, multimodal supply chain solutions. Matt Guffey (EVP and Chief U.S. Domestic Officer) added that UPS is well-positioned for data center growth due to the resiliency of its network. He also noted that the SMB growth is not just in volume, but specifically in premium air and commercial segments through the Digital Access Program.

Q : How is the new global operating model expected to drive efficiencies, and what is the status of the $3 billion cost savings program? A : Nando Cesarone (EVP and Chief Global Operations Officer) stated the goal is to build a "single intelligent transportation utility" by exporting successful US initiatives, like RFID technology (which eliminates 1.9 million scans per day), to the global network. Regarding cost savings, CFO Brian Dykes confirmed confidence in hitting the $3 billion target, noting that the final phase of the Driver Choice program (1,600 exits) and building restructurings are complete, aligning hours with the reduced Amazon volume.

Q : What are the expectations for peak season volume and network efficiency? A : CEO Carol Tome stated the network is more automated and efficient than ever, with nearly 70% of packages flowing through automated processes. While total Q4 US average daily volume is expected to be down slightly year-over-year due to the Amazon reduction, core volume is growing. CFO Brian Dykes added that by bringing down the "water level" on difficult volume, UPS can deliver a better cost peak with fewer vehicle rentals and aircraft leases.

Q : What are the major strategic decisions or challenges facing UPS over the next two years, particularly regarding labor? A : CEO Carol Tome acknowledged the upcoming Teamster contract negotiation in 2028. She emphasized the company's history of a constructive relationship with Teamster leadership, citing the mutually satisfactory outcome of the Driver Choice program. She noted that lessons learned from the 2023 negotiations position the company well for the future, and her experience as the only CEO besides the founder to negotiate two contracts is a distinct advantage.

news.Title: Amazon Plans to Spend More on AI. Here’s Why the Stock is a Once-in-a-Decade Buy Hiding in Plain Sight.
news.Content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) stocks have been driving stock market performance in recent years, and investors have cheered growth in the space. But to keep this growth story going, tech giants have to invest heavily, and that's exactly what they've been doing over the past several quarters. This investment, totaling hundreds of billions of dollars, has gone into the infrastructure build-out, with cloud players and other "hyperscalers" building data centers and furnishing them with equipment.

Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), as the owner of Amazon Web Services (AWS), is one of these players. This week, the company reported earnings that fell short of estimates, and negative free cash flow was also deeper than expected. On top of this, Amazon says it aims to "spend meaningfully more" next year.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The news sent the stock lower in the following trading session, and this is after Amazon's 14% drop from a high back in August. Now, here's why this player is a once-in-a-decade buy hiding in plain sight.

Image source: Getty Images.

Amazon's e-commerce dominance

So, first, let's catch up on the Amazon story so far and its presence in AI . This company is probably best known for its e-commerce business, as many of us shop on Amazon daily for groceries and other essentials or turn to the platform for entertainment in the form of books and movies. The Prime subscription program, offering fast delivery and other perks, has kept customers loyal and the revenue engine going.

Meanwhile, AWS has become the company's main profit driver over the years -- and now, the AI opportunity is supercharging growth. AWS is the world's No. 1 cloud services provider , making it the natural choice for customers that already use the platform for non-AI services. For AI, they come to AWS for any of their needs, from AI chips to large language models and agentic AI.

Due to this, AWS has delivered explosive growth in recent quarters, and performance in the third quarter extended this trend. The cloud unit reported 39% revenue growth to $46 billion, beating analysts' estimates.

However, to generate such growth today and into the future, Amazon has prioritized investing in the AI build-out. During the latest quarterly report, the company kept its capital spending forecast for the year at $220 billion, but as I mentioned above, it said it will keep up the aggressive spending next year. Amazon reported negative free cash flow of $42 billion in the trailing 12 months as it paid for property and equipment.

Story Continues

Concern about the future AI revenue opportunity

Investors are happy to see AI growth, but in recent months, they've started to worry that the revenue opportunity may not justify such spending levels. As a result, they've grown more cautious about AI stocks, particularly the cloud giants like Amazon that are leading the infrastructure ramp-up.

This has weighed on Amazon stock, but I think the concerns may be overdone. Here's why Amazon stock today may be a once-in-a-decade buying opportunity. And it starts with what Amazon chief Andy Jassy said this week after announcing his plans for more AI spending.

Jassy said Amazon, as it increases spending, is seeing "a clear line of sight to attractive financial returns" and that even a $184 billion annual run rate at AWS leaves plenty of room for growth. In fact, based on Amazon's innovation, additional capacity to come, and demand from customers, Jassy predicts that AWS can become a trillion-dollar revenue business within the coming five to 10 years.

If he's right, spending heavily today is clearly the right move. The strength of demand so far and the fact that AI usage is in its early stages give us reason to be optimistic about what's to come. Meanwhile, Amazon stock trades at 30x forward earnings estimates.

AMZN PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

This isn't its lowest ever, but Amazon is reasonably priced considering today's revenue levels and the strength of growth.

Of course, the path may not be completely linear, and the AI story could encounter some turbulence at certain points. As it stands, Amazon has said pressure on free cash flow would continue during this AI build-out phase. While some may hesitate to buy Amazon because of these concerns, I say the positives outweigh the negatives -- and that makes the stock a once-in-a-decade buy hiding in plain sight.

news.Title: Apar Industries Ltd (BOM:532259) (Q2 2027) Earnings Call Highlights: Profit Jumps 78% as Order ...
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Release Date: October 29, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

Consolidated revenue grew 21.3% YoY to ?6,931 crores in Q2 FY27, with domestic revenue up 34.3%.

EBITDA post forex rose 57.8% YoY to ?787 crores, with margin expanding 270 bps to 11.4%.

Net profit surged 77.8% YoY to ?447 crores, and PAT margin improved by 200 bps.

Conductor order book reached an all-time high of ?12,025 crores, including new premium orders like Z-shaped conductors and high-fiber OPGW.

Cable division order book strong at ?3,000 crores, with ~?1,000 crores from data center projects (Google, Amazon).

Oil division EBITDA grew 185% YoY to ?299 crores, with margin at ?23,262/KL vs ?6,517/KL last year.

QIP of ?2,500 crores completed, improving financial flexibility and credit rating upgraded to AA.

Industry tailwinds: India added 8,775 ckm of transmission lines (+153% YoY) and approved new green transmission corridors.

Cable capacity utilization >90%, with some sections at 100-105%, and expansion on track.

Management expects H2 FY27 to be stronger with volume recovery and execution catch-up.

Negative Points

Conductor volume declined 9.2% YoY in Q2 due to delays in manufacturing clearances and order awards from TBCB customers.

US revenue declined 29.7% YoY in Q2 due to ?800 crores of goods in transit (DDP basis) not recognized.

Oil division volume fell 20% YoY as company deliberately limited sales to manage credit risk amid volatile base oil prices.

Cable export revenue dropped 29.8% QoQ and export mix fell to 19% from 42.3% last year due to lower US sales.

High commodity inflation (aluminum up 35-40%, copper up 50%, base oil up 100%) impacted working capital and margins.

Freight rates spiked in Q2, especially to Europe and LatAm, though showing signs of reversal in Q3.

CTC capacity was affected by heavy rains in Silvassa, losing ~20 days of production in Q2.

Competition from Chinese exporters remains severe due to SHFE-LME arbitrage, impacting standard product margins.

Domestic CTC margins may see a slight drop as new capacity comes on stream.

Oil division margins are not sustainable at current levels due to one-off inventory gains and volatile environment.

Q & A Highlights

Q : With H1 FY27 EBITDA per tonne already averaging Rs 48,000-50,000 versus your earlier guidance of around Rs 40,000, how should we think about conductor profitability for the year, and where is the premiumization coming from? A : Ramesh Iyer (CFO) said the premium mix was high in both Q1 and Q2, but margins vary by product, geography and customer, so exact EBITDA per tonne is hard to estimate; the base range remains Rs 35,000-36,000 plus tailwinds. Kushal Desai (Chairman & MD) added that first-time wins like the Z-shaped conductor for a Scandinavian offshore wind farm (made by only two other global manufacturers) and the turnkey 48-fiber OPGW order from Karnataka (using Nokia-partnered IP-MPLS technology) point to continued premiumization, though metal and freight volatility persists.

Story Continues

Q : Conductor volumes fell 9.2% in Q2 due to delayed manufacturing clearances and TBCB order awards. Have clearances started improving, and what volume growth do you expect in H2? A : Ramesh Iyer (CFO) said the trend is reversing, with Q3 and Q4 being peak execution seasons and customers facing finite timelines; the decline should be arrested by next quarter and H2 volumes should be stronger than H1. Kushal Desai (Chairman & MD) noted TBCB awards carry a maximum 36-month execution window with stringent penalties, and existing-contract execution hit an all-time high (transmission line addition up 153% YoY), so new project work cannot be postponed indefinitely.

Q : US revenue appears weak this quarter. What is driving this, and when will it normalize? A : Kushal Desai (Chairman & MD) explained that roughly Rs 800 crore of conductors and cables sold on a DDP basis were in transit at quarter-end due to shipping and container delays, all destined for the US. This caused US revenue to show a 29.7% decline, but the sales will be recognized in Q3, when the picture should look different; the order book remains very strong.

Q : Oil division volumes fell about 20% YoY even as EBITDA surged 185%. What is the operating philosophy, and are these margins sustainable? A : Kushal Desai (Chairman & MD) said the company deliberately limits sales given record refining margin spreads and base oil prices that have roughly doubled, which strains customer payment capacity. Apar has shifted to contract-based base oil purchases, higher-margin grades and consistent customers, accepting lower volumes to protect cash flow and ROCE. He cautioned that current margins are by no means normal, though some inventory gains did accrue in Q2.

Q : The cable order book has jumped to about Rs 3,000 crore, helped by data center orders. How large can data centers become, and do they carry better margins? A : Kushal Desai (Chairman & MD) said about Rs 1,000 crore of the order book is from the Google US data center (over Rs 500 crore, the largest single US order) and Amazon's largest India data center, with more expected. US data center cables carry better margins due to higher specifications, while India offers a larger addressable market but lower margins amid greater competition; GPU-based AI data centers will eventually raise Indian specifications too.

Q : What is the outlook for the HTLS/reconductoring opportunity, and is the margin on HTLS higher than the segment average? A : Apar's management said many HTLS tenders have been issued but processing through utility board approvals has taken time; competition is rising, but the overall pie is growing, so volumes and revenue should hold even if market share dips. Kushal Desai (Chairman & MD) highlighted CEA's new 10-15% thermal margin limits and n-1 reliability mandate in India, plus the US SPARC program ($1.9 billion federal funding, 31 projects, 23 GW unlocked), as strong structural drivers for reconductoring, where Apar is the world's largest HTLS player.

Q : What is the outlook for CTC conductors, including exports and margins? A : Kushal Desai (Chairman & MD) said CTC demand continues to grow, with CEA considering wider usage in transformers; Apar has trial orders from the US, advanced talks in Europe and existing Middle East customers. Q2 output was hit by heavy rains at Silvassa, costing about 20 of 90 days of capacity. Margins are broadly similar to the segment average, with domestic margins likely to soften slightly as new industry capacity comes on stream, while specialized 400kV/765kV and HVDC products should command premiums.

Q : Trade payables days fell to about 81 from 109 in March 2026. Is this due to QIP deployment or higher vendor payouts? A : Ramesh Iyer (CFO) said the Rs 2,500 crore QIP proceeds were deployed into working capital, including cash purchases of raw materials, which lowered payable days. Customer acceptances stood at around Rs 3,500 crore as of September 2026.

Q : What is the CapEx plan for FY27 and beyond, and what is the Rs 1,000 crore enabling investment in the Singapore subsidiary (PSPL) for? A : Ramesh Iyer (CFO) said the domestic CapEx program is about Rs 1,500 crore to be spent over 12-15 months, of which roughly Rs 500 crore is already spent; after this phase, annual CapEx should normalize to Rs 300-400 crore. Kushal Desai (Chairman & MD) clarified the PSPL resolution is an enabling provision for the wholly owned Singapore entity, aimed at overseas expansion, with details to be disclosed to exchanges at the appropriate time.

Q : What are the capacity utilization levels across divisions, and is capacity a constraint? A : Kushal Desai (Chairman & MD) said cable utilization exceeds 90%, with copper cable sections serving data centers running at 100-105%; conductors are at about 80% with expansion underway each quarter; oil is not capacity constrained. He said capacity will not be the main constraint going into next year, with operating discipline and customer clearances being the limiting factors.
