news.Title: Marvell may buy its own laser supplier as investors pull back
news.Content:
Every video call you join and every chatbot answer you get travels part of its trip as laser light. Marvell Technology (MRVL) makes chips that work alongside many of those lasers.

Lumentum Holdings (LITE) makes many of the lasers, and it can't keep up. CEO Michael Hurlston said this month its optical parts are sold out through early 2029, Bloomberg reported .

Marvell may have found a permanent fix. The chipmaker, which already buys lasers from Lumentum, is in advanced talks to buy the company, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. A deal could come as soon as next week, though nothing is signed.

Marvell's investors pulled back hard. The stock fell about 13% on Thursday, October 29, 2026.

The problem is size. Lumentum was worth about $83 billion before the report. Marvell held about $3.9 billion in cash at the end of its latest quarter, according to its earnings release .

Also read: Bank of America tweaks Marvell stock target after key Analyst Day

Bloomberg reported that Marvell would likely pay in shares. I understand why Marvell wants to own its bottleneck. I'm far less comfortable with the currency.

Marvell's shareholders started paying on Thursday

An all-stock deal moves the risk onto Marvell's share price. Lumentum holders would be paid in Marvell stock, so every drop in its share price shrinks the offer.

Marvell's market value ended Thursday near $191 billion . Bloomberg had valued it at about $221 billion before the report. The one-session loss comes to roughly $29 billion .

That loss alone equals more than a third of Lumentum's entire value. To me, Marvell's owners took a takeover-sized hit without seeing a single term.

Lumentum's stock told the same story. Its shares rose as much as 7% on Thursday. By the close, the gain had shrunk to less than 1%.

I read that fade as the market marking down the premium in real time. When the buyer pays in stock, a falling stock means a smaller prize.

Owning a supplier could cost Marvell some customers

The deeper risk may not be the price. In 2023, Lumentum bought Cloud Light, a maker of optical transceiver modules, for about $750 million, according to a company filing .

Rival module makers buy Marvell's signal-processing chips. After a deal, Marvell would own a competitor to some of its own customers.

Stifel estimated that Marvell holds 60% to 65% of the market for one key type of those chips, according to Seeking Alpha . The firm warned that a merger could cost Marvell share if rival module makers switch suppliers.

RBC Capital Markets still said a combination "makes strategic sense given the highly complementary product portfolios," according to Seeking Alpha. It also noted that Marvell outsources its chipmaking, while Lumentum runs its own laser fabs. Combining the two could make margins swing more, RBC warned.

Story Continues

Stifel said the closing would likely take time and require approval from both U.S. and Chinese regulators, according to Investing.com . It also listed building a scaled-up U.S. transceiver supplier, given possible limits on Chinese modules, as one of the deal's drivers.

A deal built partly around limits on Chinese modules may still need Beijing's sign-off. That irony is what I'd watch most closely.

More Artificial Intelligence:

AI's biggest business opportunity may not look like AI

AI racks are outgrowing old power: 2 chipmakers have a strategy

BofA splits software into winners and losers as AI agents arrive

What the deal could mean for both stocks

Marvell entered the week as a big 2026 winner. The stock set an intraday all-time high of $329.88 in June. Its 52-week low of $70.69 shows how fast that run came.

The 47 analysts at StockAnalysis rate Marvell a Strong Buy . Their average target of $340.56 sits far above Thursday's close. Piper Sandler and Stifel kept Buy ratings that day.

Lumentum's climb has been even steeper. Its all-time low was about $14 in October 2015. Its intraday record of $1,143 came on October 9, 2026.

The 28 analysts at StockAnalysis rate Lumentum a Buy . Their average target of $1,166 was last updated before the deal talks, so it reflects the business, not a buyout.

Thursday's nearly flat close suggests the market isn't counting on a rich Lumentum premium. Three things will settle it:

The exchange ratio will show how much of the combined company Lumentum holders would own.

Lumentum's quarterly results are expected Thursday, November 5, 2026, according to a press release .

Plans for Cloud Light will show whether Marvell intends to compete with its chip customers.

If I owned Marvell, I wouldn't sell into Thursday's drop, but I wouldn't add until the terms are public. For Lumentum, I'd wait for the November 5 report before buying.

Scarce lasers could change how chipmakers shop

When a part gets this scarce, buyers stop haggling over supply and start buying the supplier. Stifel listed securing laser supply among this deal's drivers.

With Lumentum sold out into 2029, chip designers that need lasers are negotiating from a position of weakness. If Marvell signs, I expect investors to view every independent laser maker as a supplier a chip giant can't do without.

news.Title: Big Tech Stocks Have Never Looked Cheaper. Is the Magnificent Seven a Screaming Buy?
news.Content:
Following another sell-off in tech stocks, the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) is now on the verge of a correction as the index is down roughly 8% from its closing peak.

On Friday, the trigger was underwhelming earnings reports from a slew of tech companies like Amazon , Intel , and Sandisk , offering the latest evidence that investors have grown weary with the AI trade .

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Amazon joined its hyperscaler peers like Alphabet , Microsoft , and Meta Platforms in falling in response to earnings, a sign that investors have become skeptical of the massive capital spending taking place in the cloud computing industry. Combined, these four companies are set to spend more than $700 billion this year. The world has never seen an infrastructure build-out of that size.

Though these stocks have all fallen this earnings season, their profits continue to grow, meaning many of them are as cheap as they've ever been. All four hyperscalers are reporting record profits, and, except for Microsoft, they're all trading at substantial discounts from their recent peaks.

AMZN data by YCharts

How cheap are the hyperscalers?

Assessing the valuation of these stocks isn't so easy. With the exception of Microsoft, they don't adjust their earnings to reflect one-time events, so reported earnings per share doesn't offer a clear picture of profits. Alphabet and Amazon, for example, both made large gains in their investments in Anthropic this year.

If we use operating income instead, we can get a better sense of their valuations.

AMZN EBIT (TTM) data by YCharts

Combined, these companies had roughly $490 billion in operating income in the last year, including Amazon's most recent quarter. Their total market cap is now $11.5 trillion, meaning they trade altogether at 23.5 times operating income, which is similar to the S&P 500 .

Image source: Getty Images.

Why are big tech stocks so cheap?

The simple explanation for why these stocks have gotten so cheap is that all four of these, except Microsoft, are now burning cash to fund their AI build-outs, and investors have gotten spooked by the risk in that investment.

AMZN Free Cash Flow (Quarterly) data by YCharts

Updated for the third quarter, Amazon's free cash flow dropped to a loss of $34.8 billion.

Even though three out of four of these stocks have large, highly profitable cloud computing businesses that can monetize that spend, the AI industry is still new, and long-term demand is uncertain.

Story Continues

Is it time to buy the hyperscaler stocks?

All four of these companies are growing revenue well into the double digits, as the chart below shows.

They have continued to defy the law of large numbers and are delivering growth rates rarely seen for the biggest companies on the market, which are typically mature businesses.

Those growth rates should also assuage concerns about their ability to earn a return on their capital investments, especially as Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet have all seen growth dramatically accelerate in their cloud divisions.

Meta does not currently have a cloud business, but the company could launch one, as CEO Mark Zuckerberg has openly discussed it. In addition to its rapidly growing advertising business, Meta has promising growth businesses in smart glasses and Muse, its new personal AI agent, and it likely has more in the pipeline.

Overall, these stocks are making record profits and are well-positioned to lead the AI boom, which is why they're investing heavily in it. For them to trade at a similar multiple to the S&P 500 when they're growing much faster than the index and with larger profit margins is a mistake. Investors should take advantage of the double-digit discount in these stocks and scoop them up while they're cheap.

news.Title: MPWR Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Demand and Capacity Expansion
news.Content:
Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. MPWR emphasized accelerating enterprise data demand, expanding production capacity and broader customer diversification during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call.

Third-quarter non-GAAP earnings reached $8.19 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $7.80. Revenues of $1.20 billion also surpassed the $1.16 billion consensus expectation.

Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. Quote

Management outlined growth opportunities across AI infrastructure, communications, automotive and robotics while addressing margin sustainability, operating leverage and emerging power architectures.

MPWR Raises Enterprise Data Growth Expectations

CFO Tony Balow raised the company's 2026 enterprise data revenue growth floor to 150% year over year from 130%, reflecting stronger demand across existing and newer customers.

Enterprise data revenues climbed 164.6% year over year to $506.7 million, supported by AI and server power management solutions.

Responding to Needham's questions, Balow emphasized customer diversification, growing adoption of higher-value power modules and increasing content per platform. He expects these drivers to continue into 2027, although management withheld specific annual growth projections.

Monolithic Power Expands Capacity for Future Demand

Balow confirmed that annual revenue-supporting capacity exceeded $6 billion during the quarter. Management expects capacity to reach $8 billion by the second half of 2027, progressing toward $10 billion.

Responding to StoneX, Balow clarified that capacity expansion is intended to stay ahead of customer requirements rather than signal a specific revenue trajectory.

He also told Wells Fargo that the company's fabless manufacturing model supports additional capacity without substantial increases in capital intensity.

MPWR Sees Communications Growth Extending Into 2027

Communications revenues advanced 134.7% year over year to $187.4 million, reflecting demand for optical module and networking switch power solutions.

Balow identified communications as the company's second-fastest-growing end market in 2026. Responding to Needham, he attributed accelerating growth to contributions from both optical modules and switches.

Management expects continued opportunities from the transition toward 1.6-terabit optical modules and additional switch design wins. Balow emphasized that these developments create opportunities for higher content alongside volume growth.

Story Continues

Monolithic Power Details Automotive and Robotics Expansion

Automotive revenues increased 19.2% year over year to $180.7 million, driven partly by advanced driver-assistance system power solutions.

Balow highlighted initial orders for 48-volt products and expanding customer adoption of zonal vehicle architectures. Responding to Wells Fargo, he emphasized geographically diversified demand and identified these architectural transitions as growth drivers for 2027.

Founder, chairman, president and CEO Michael Hsing also discussed emerging robotics opportunities. Sensor and motor-control products have begun generating revenues across multiple geographies, while Balow characterized 2026 primarily as a period of accumulating design wins.

MPWR Addresses Margins and Emerging Power Technologies

Balow reaffirmed management's preferred non-GAAP gross margin range of 55% to 60%, emphasizing gradual expansion rather than abrupt pricing-driven increases.

Responding to Truist Securities, he also highlighted operating leverage as revenue growth outpaced expense expansion. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 38.6%, compared with 35.4% a year earlier.

Management discussed gallium nitride solutions under evaluation for 800-volt data center architectures. Hsing emphasized reliability requirements, while Balow indicated initial architectural ramps around late 2027, with broader adoption anticipated in 2028.

Monolithic Power Outlines Q4 Expectations

Management projected fourth-quarter revenues between $1.315 billion and $1.385 billion, with non-GAAP gross margin ranging from 55.5% to 56.1%.

Non-GAAP operating expenses are expected to be between $216.8 million and $220.8 million. These projections accompany continued investment in product development and manufacturing support.

MPWR Maintains a Diversified Growth Focus

Management's overarching message emphasized expanding beyond established power management applications while maintaining disciplined spending and reliable customer supply.

Hsing expressed confidence in continued growth, while Balow emphasized customer diversification and capacity readiness. The company also repurchased $453.4 million of shares during the third quarter.

Monolithic Power's Zacks Rank & Style Scores Signal Mixed Prospects

MPWR currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), indicating favorable near-term earnings estimate revision characteristics. Its Momentum Score of A highlights attractive price momentum, while its Growth Score of C indicates a more moderate growth-style assessment. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

However, the Value Score of F and VGM Score of D reflect weaker valuation characteristics and an unfavorable combined style profile. These scores temper the stock's overall attractiveness under the Zacks framework. The Zacks Rank remains subject to change as analysts revise earnings estimates following the latest results.

news.Title: Adobe Drops 29% YTD: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
Adobe ADBE shares have dropped 29.1% year to date (YTD), underperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's return of 17.5%. The weakness appears to reflect investor concerns over intensifying competition from AI-native creative platforms, uncertainty surrounding AI monetization, modest recurring revenue growth, pressure on profitability and leadership transition risks.

The company has been playing a catch-up role in the AI domain, not only against established players like Microsoft MSFT, Alphabet GOOGL and Salesforce CRM, but also from AI-native companies like OpenAI, Midjourney and Canva. YTD, Adobe shares have underperformed Alphabet's 9.3% drop, Salesforce's decline of 12.8% and Microsoft's appreciation of 9.7%. So, what should investors do with Adobe stock? Let's find out.

ADBE Stock's Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Adobe Faces Multiple Challenges

The rapid proliferation of AI-powered content creation tools is challenging Adobe's traditional competitive advantages in creative software. AI-native platforms capable of generating images, videos, designs and marketing content through natural-language prompts are reducing dependence on traditional creative applications such as Photoshop, Illustrator and Premiere. Adobe is responding by embedding conversational AI and autonomous creative agents into its flagship applications. However, investors remain concerned that generative AI could commoditize certain creative workflows, increase pricing pressure and weaken ADBE's ability to sustain premium subscription pricing.

Meanwhile, AI-first ending Annualized Recurring Revenue (ARR) exceeded $650 million and surged more than 150% year over year. AI-first offerings still represent a relatively small portion of the overall recurring revenue base. Adobe expects ARR growth of 10.2% by the end of fiscal 2026, suggesting that strong adoption of new AI offerings has yet to meaningfully accelerate companywide recurring revenue growth. Investors have been skeptical about how quickly increasing usage of Firefly, AI Assistant and agentic workflows will translate into sustained revenue acceleration.

Adobe expects fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 revenues between $6.80 billion and $6.85 billion, implying approximately 1% sequential growth at the midpoint. The guidance suggests relatively modest near-term sequential revenue momentum despite rapidly growing AI engagement. Adobe also projects a non-GAAP operating margin of approximately 44% for the fiscal fourth quarter, below its fiscal 2026 target of approximately 45%. Continued investments in AI infrastructure, product development and customer acquisition could constrain margin expansion over the near term.

Story Continues

Adobe's Earnings Estimate Revision Trend Steady

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2026 earnings is currently pegged at $24.47 per share, unchanged over the past 60 days, indicating 16.86% growth from the figure reported in fiscal 2025. The consensus mark for fiscal 2026 revenues is currently pegged at $26.6 billion, suggesting 11.92% growth from the figure reported in fiscal 2025.

Adobe Inc. Price and Consensus

Adobe Inc. price-consensus-chart | Adobe Inc. Quote

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings is currently pegged at $6.32 per share, up a couple of cents over the past 60 days, indicating 14.91% growth from the figure reported in fiscal 2025. The consensus mark for fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 revenues is currently pegged at $6.84 billion, suggesting 10.38% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Adobe's Prospects Ride on Growing AI-Monetization

Adobe's AI push is gaining traction. The company's expanding Firefly ecosystem offers significant long-term growth potential as demand for AI-generated images, videos, audio and marketing content increases. Growing AI credit consumption across Creative Cloud and Firefly indicates increasing customer engagement. Adobe has also introduced AI-powered creative agents across Photoshop and Premiere, enabling users to automate repetitive workflows and improve productivity.

Adobe's Business Professionals and Consumers segment represents an attractive growth opportunity, driven by increasing adoption of Acrobat AI Assistant, Adobe Express and AI-powered document productivity solutions. Adobe's integration with ChatGPT, Claude, Chrome and Microsoft Edge expands product accessibility. New capabilities such as Adobe Productivity Agent, Knowledge Base and Analyzer strengthen Acrobat's appeal among enterprises and business professionals, creating opportunities for higher subscription conversion and cross-selling.

Meanwhile, Adobe Experience Platform, Adobe GenStudio and Adobe Experience Manager are benefiting from increasing enterprise investments in personalized marketing, content automation and customer experience orchestration. Growing enterprise demand for automated marketing workflows and AI-powered customer engagement solutions should support recurring revenue growth and strengthen Adobe's competitive position. Adobe's expanding freemium user base offers substantial opportunities to convert users into paying subscribers. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, monthly active users across its creativity and productivity businesses exceeded one billion, increasing more than 20% year over year.

Adobe Trades at a Discount

Adobe currently has a Value Score of B, which suggests the stock is trading at a discount.

In terms of forward 12-month price/earnings (P/E), Adobe shares are trading at 9.05X, lower than the broader sector's 19.39X, Microsoft's 25.40X, Alphabet's 17.76X and Salesforce's 14.34X.

ADBE Stock's Valuation

Conclusion

Adobe's 29% YTD share-price decline reflects concerns surrounding AI disruption, relatively modest ARR growth, uncertainty over monetization and potential margin pressures. Nevertheless, the company's expanding Firefly ecosystem, growing adoption of Acrobat AI, strengthening enterprise customer experience portfolio and robust cash generation provide meaningful long-term opportunities.

ADBE currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), which implies that investors should wait for a more favorable point to accumulate the stock. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: If the AI Bubble Scare Gets Worse, This Is the Chip Stock I'd Still Hold
news.Content:
As the market's fears of an artificial intelligence (AI) bubble grow, investors would be well advised to focus on companies that have real earnings, durable competitive advantages , and exposure to long-term demand. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) stands out for its dominance in chip manufacturing, making it one of the strongest stocks to hold even if the AI hype fades.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

TSM gives investors AI exposure without tying them to one chip designer

Chipmakers like Nvidia and AMD continue to design processors capable of handling ever more demanding computing workloads. What most of the designers don't do is manufacture them in-house. Churning out high-end chips at scale requires specialized technology, expertise, and foundries that are neither cheap nor easy to build.

That's where Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing comes in.

TSM runs the world's largest third-party foundry business, manufacturing chips designed by its customers for use not only in AI, but also in smartphones and other electronics.

It's one of the few that has the technological capability to produce the advanced, transistor-dense chips that power the AI industry, so essentially all of the leading designers make use of its services. As a result, TSM's success is not tied to the success of any single AI application or chip designer.

This business model gives TSM shareholders broad exposure to the AI race, and spares them from having to predict which chip designers will emerge as its biggest winners. That advantage will matter even more if and when investor sentiment toward the sector turns sour.

Even if the market begins to question the valuations of individual AI stocks, demand for chip manufacturing could remain strong as businesses continue to develop and deploy compute-heavy technologies.

That said, TSM would not be immune to an AI sector downturn. If data center customers and other chip-using businesses cut their spending or delay orders, the foundry giant could feel the effects. TSM also faces geopolitical risks because its manufacturing base is concentrated in Taiwan, where a conflict with China could disrupt production.

The opportunity extends beyond Nvidia's GPUs

Graphics processing units (GPUs) are essential to training and running AI models. But as AI systems become more advanced, demand for compute power is spreading across several chip categories. Agentic AI workloads, for example, require data centers to have a larger proportion of central processing units (CPUs). And hyperscalers are also designing and deploying larger numbers of application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) that are custom-built to handle their AI workloads.

Story Continues

TSM is well positioned to benefit from this diversifying demand because it manufactures all of those types of chips.

If AI adoption continues to expand into enterprise software, consumer devices, and other applications, chip demand could remain healthy even if investor sentiment toward top AI companies weakens. TSM doesn't need every AI application to succeed; it just needs enough customers to keep investing in advanced chips.

Its next-generation manufacturing technology creates further growth opportunities

Beyond the chips themselves, TSM is also investing heavily in its manufacturing technology.

It began volume production using its 2-nanometer (2nm) process node in the fourth quarter of 2025. But the company continues to improve its manufacturing technology, with volume production for its N2P and A16 nodes ramping up in the second half of 2026. Its longer-term roadmap includes the even more powerful A14 process node, which is expected to enter volume production in 2028.

These steady advancements are important because AI developers demand chips that can deliver more compute without letting power consumption and operating costs spiral out of control.

For investors worried about how long the AI boom can last, TSM's roadmap offers a reason to look beyond short-term sentiment. The company is investing in manufacturing capabilities to support future generations of advanced chips, rather than relying on a single product cycle, which makes TSM much more resilient to cracks in the AI bubble.

But how do analysts and the valuation view the stock?

What analysts and valuation say about investing in TSM

Wall Street remains bullish on TSM: Among 19 analysts covering the stock, 16 rate it a strong buy, two a buy, and just one a hold. Their average price target, meanwhile, suggests 23% potential upside over the next year. And based on its current price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of over 27, investors are expecting AI-driven chip demand to continue fueling growth.

The company's manufacturing expertise and strong position in the AI supply chain give it a compelling long-term bull case. With that, TSM may be one of the strongest ways to invest in AI, even if fears that the sector is in a bubble intensify.

news.Title: GOOGL Drops 13% Post Q3 Earnings: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
Alphabet GOOGL shares plunged 12.64% on Thursday, following the release of third-quarter 2026 results, wiping out $482 billion in market capitalization. The selloff reflected concerns over slowing Google Search advertising growth, weaker monetization of AI-powered searches, mounting AI infrastructure expenditures, negative free cash flow and disappointing earnings. Although Alphabet delivered 25% year-over-year revenue growth and Google Cloud revenues more than doubled, investors questioned whether the company's massive AI investments would generate sufficient returns to offset pressure on its core advertising business. Let's dig deep to find out.

GOOGL Stock Suffers From Multiple Challenges

Google Search and other advertising revenues increased 12% year over year to $63.35 billion in the third quarter, decelerating from approximately 17% growth in the second quarter. The revenue figure also missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 2.53%. This slowdown was particularly concerning because Search remains Alphabet's largest revenue contributor and provides significant cash flows to fund AI investments. GOOGL acknowledged that growing AI Mode usage contributed to Search revenue deceleration because AI Mode queries currently generate lower monetization than traditional searches.

Alphabet's capital expenditures surged 114% year over year to $51.36 billion in the third quarter of 2026, exceeding operating cash flow of $42.29 billion. Consequently, free cash flow deteriorated to negative $9.07 billion from positive $24.46 billion a year earlier. Trailing 12-month free cash flow declined 73% year over year to $19.75 billion. Alphabet maintained its 2026 capital expenditure guidance of $195-$205 billion and expects spending to increase significantly in 2027.

Meanwhile, the company's aggressive AI expansion is increasing its financial obligations. At the end of September 2026, GOOGL reported approximately $924 billion in future purchase commitments and $152 billion in pre-commencement leases and other obligations, representing more than $1 trillion in maximum contractual commitments. Alphabet cautioned that flexible pricing and volume terms could reduce actual spending. Long-term debt increased to $125.1 billion from $46.5 billion at the end of 2025. Alphabet also raised approximately $12.4 billion through common stock issuance during the third quarter and $28.7 billion through senior unsecured notes.

Apart from risks associated with the huge AI-related capital expenditure, Alphabet's prospects suffer from intensifying competition from the likes of Microsoft MSFT, Amazon AMZN, OpenAI, Anthropic, Apple AAPL and Meta across its operational footprint. Year to date (YTD), Alphabet shares have dropped 9.3%, underperforming Apple's 28.4%, Microsoft's 9.7% and Amazon's 5.7% returns.

Story Continues

GOOGL Stock's Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Alphabet is facing stiff competition in the cloud computing space from Microsoft and Amazon. Despite Google Cloud revenues increasing 103% year over year to $30.71 billion, investors remain concerned about the sustainability and profitability of this growth. TPU system sales contributed meaningfully to Cloud revenues. Alphabet also expects near-term Google Cloud margin headwinds as it expands the use of third-party compute capacity to address infrastructure constraints. Higher depreciation, energy expenses and data center operating costs are expected to weigh on profitability.

GOOGL Shares Are Overvalued

Alphabet shares are overvalued, as suggested by a Value Score of C.

GOOGL stock is trading at a forward 12-month price/sales (P/E) of 6.43X, a premium compared with the broader sector's 5.60X and Amazon's 2.82X.

However, Alphabet shares are trading at a discount compared with Microsoft and Apple, shares of which are trading at a P/S multiple of 9.50 and 9.69, respectively.

GOOGL Stock's Valuation

GOOGL's Prospects Ride on Cloud & AI Initiatives

Alphabet's Google Cloud business remains a significant long-term growth driver, supported by accelerating enterprise investments in AI infrastructure, cloud modernization and agentic AI applications. Google Cloud's backlog reached $561 billion, with Alphabet expecting to recognize slightly more than 55% of the backlog as revenue over the next 24 months. Strong enterprise demand for AI infrastructure, core GCP services, Gemini Enterprise, BigQuery and cybersecurity solutions strengthens Alphabet's long-term revenue visibility.

Alphabet's expanding Gemini ecosystem is a key long-term growth catalyst. The Gemini app surpassed one billion users, while first-party model APIs processed nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, up 40% sequentially and more than fourfold year over year. The introduction of Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon strengthens Alphabet's positioning in advanced reasoning, coding, cybersecurity and enterprise automation. The integration of Gemini across Search, Chrome, Android, Workspace and Google Cloud provides multiple opportunities to monetize AI through advertising, subscriptions, enterprise software and developer services.

Despite near-term monetization challenges, Alphabet's growing AI Search engagement presents a significant long-term opportunity. The company reported its fastest year-over-year Search query growth in five years, while AI Mode queries averaged three times the length of traditional searches. Alphabet is expanding advertising within AI Overviews and AI Mode, including international availability and multiturn ads. AI Max and Performance Max are also strengthening advertiser capabilities through improved targeting, automated campaign optimization and AI-generated creative assets.

However, the transition from traditional search results to AI-generated responses presents a structural challenge to Alphabet's largest revenue-generating business. Competition from OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude and other AI-powered discovery platforms could further disrupt traditional search behavior. This doesn't bode well for GOOGL's prospects.

2026 Earnings Estimate Revisions Positive for GOOGL Stock

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings is pegged at $20.60 per share, up by a nickel over the past 30 days, indicating 90.6% growth from the figure reported in 2025.

Alphabet Inc. Price and Consensus

Alphabet Inc. price-consensus-chart | Alphabet Inc. Quote

The consensus mark for fourth-quarter 2026 earnings is pegged at $3.25 per share, up by a penny over the past 30 days, suggesting 15.3% year-over-year growth.

Conclusion

Alphabet's sharp post-earnings decline reflects growing concerns over slowing Search advertising growth, lower monetization of AI-powered queries and mounting infrastructure investments that are pressuring free cash flow. Although robust Google Cloud growth, expanding TPU adoption, Gemini innovation and a substantial backlog support long-term growth prospects, GOOGL's aggressive capital spending, rising financing requirements and uncertain AI monetization economics warrant caution. Investors should closely monitor improvements in Search monetization, Cloud profitability and free cash flow before becoming more constructive on GOOGL stock.

Alphabet currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Here’s What a $10,000 Investment in TSMC Stock Will Be Worth by 2030
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM), popularly known as TSMC, is one of the most important companies in the semiconductor ecosystem, as it is the world's largest semiconductor foundry, manufacturing chips for other companies.

TSMC doesn't design any chips of its own. It manufactures chips for fabless chipmakers, including Nvidia , Advanced Micro Devices , and Broadcom , as well as consumer electronics giants such as Apple and Sony . The chips made by TSMC find their way into multiple applications, such as data center servers, vehicles, personal computers, and smartphones.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Not surprisingly, TSMC stock has been an outstanding investment in recent years. A $10,000 investment made in TSMC five years ago is now worth over $38,000. The good news is that it isn't too late to buy this semiconductor stock. Let's look at the reasons why it is a good idea to put $10,000 into TSMC even after the terrific gains it has clocked over the past five years.

Image source: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing.

TSMC's addressable market is getting bigger

TSMC dominates the global pure-play foundry market with an estimated market share of 73%, according to Counterpoint Research. However, TSMC is now more than just a pure-play foundry company. It also provides advanced packaging, testing, and photomasking services. TSMC calls this expanded market Foundry 2.0, which encompasses the overall semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem, excluding memory chips.

Counterpoint Research notes that the global Foundry 2.0 market's revenue increased by an impressive 25% year over year in Q2 to $96.6 billion, up from the 24% increase in Q1. TSMC is the biggest player in Foundry 2.0, controlling 42% of this space in Q2. Notably, TSMC's share of the Foundry 2.0 market has increased from 38% at the end of 2025.

Even better, Counterpoint Research expects TSMC's Foundry 2.0 revenue to grow by 50% year over year in the second half of 2026, implying an improvement over the 34% revenue growth seen in Q2. So, TSMC's share of the Foundry 2.0 market is likely to get even better by the end of the year.

Importantly, the Foundry 2.0 market is anticipated to keep growing at a healthy pace over the long run. Market research firm IDC expects the Foundry 2.0 market's revenue to exceed $360 billion in 2026. Even better, the firm expects this market to clock a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 11% through 2030, indicating that TSMC's addressable opportunity could increase to almost $550 billion by the end of the decade.

Story Continues

I won't be surprised to see TSMC's Foundry 2.0 share increasing further by the end of the decade, driven by the strong demand for its advanced chip manufacturing. Specifically, TSMC sees demand for its advanced manufacturing nodes used in artificial intelligence (AI) applications increasing at a high 50% CAGR through 2029.

So, there is a strong chance that TSMC will outpace the broader market over the next four years. Also, the stronger market share will improve TSMC's pricing power. The foundry giant is expected to implement price hikes of up to 10% in 2027, as Reuters reported in July. TSMC is therefore on track to benefit from strong volumes and favorable pricing, which should ensure robust top- and bottom-line growth for the company.

Here's why it is a good idea to invest $10,000 in this stock

TSMC's dominant position in the foundry market, the secular growth of this space, and the price hikes that it is on track to implement explain why the company's earnings are poised to increase at a nice pace through 2028.

TSM EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

According to the chart above, TSMC's earnings could jump by 34% next year and by 27% in 2028. For comparison, its earnings are projected to jump by 64% this year. However, don't be surprised to see TSMC's earnings per share (EPS) growth outpacing the market's expectations in the future. Analysts have already raised their long-term EPS growth estimates and may become more bullish given the factors discussed above.

TSM EPS LT Growth Estimates data by YCharts

Assuming TSMC's earnings increase by 40% a year in 2029 and 2030, its EPS could jump to $58.45 by the end of the decade (using 2028's projected EPS of $29.82 as the base). If this semiconductor stock trades at even 19 times earnings at that time, in line with the S&P 500 index's forward earnings multiple, its price could reach $1,110, implying 153% upside.

So, a $10,000 investment in TSMC right now could be worth more than $25,000 by 2030, suggesting investors can still consider buying this semiconductor giant in anticipation of further gains.

news.Title: BofA Says Wall Street May Be Misreading Apple
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Apple ( AAPL ) heads into fiscal fourth-quarter earnings with a new concern hanging over Wall Street estimates: the company's staggered iPhone launch may be distorting how analysts model revenue and margins across the next several quarters.

Is AAPL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan said consensus expectations could be mismodeled after Apple split its latest iPhone rollout between the September and March quarters.

The iPhone Pro, Pro Max and Duo launched in September, while the base model and Air are scheduled for March.

That timing shift matters because it can pull more premium-device revenue into one quarter while pushing lower-priced volume into another, complicating year-over-year comparisons and margin forecasts.

Mohan said Bank of America is taking a more conservative view overall.

The firm now models 247 million iPhone units for fiscal 2027 , down by 9 million units from its prior estimate and below the roughly 260 million units implied by Wall Street consensus.

For Apple's fiscal fourth quarter, BofA expects $113 billion in revenue and $1.97 in EPS , versus consensus estimates of about $114 billion and $1.99.

The bigger disconnect may come in the December and March quarters.

Mohan believes Wall Street is too optimistic on December-quarter revenue and March-quarter gross margins, while potentially underestimating June-quarter revenue because of the shifted launch schedule.

Component costs are another key issue.

Apple has raised prices in response to higher component inflation, while investors will be watching whether those increases are enough to protect margins.

BofA also noted that residual tariff refunds and memory inventory could create upside to its more conservative near-term margin assumptions.

The firm still maintains a Buy rating and $370 price target on Apple.

Investor takeaway

I think the most interesting part of BofA's note is not simply that its iPhone unit estimate is lower.

It is the argument that the timing of Apple's earnings may now matter almost as much as the absolute level of demand .

A staggered launch can make one quarter look weaker and another stronger without necessarily changing the full-year economics by the same amount.

That creates a real risk of investors overreacting to quarterly misses or beats that are partly driven by product timing rather than underlying demand.

For investors, the key things to watch are December-quarter revenue, March gross margins, iPhone unit trends, component costs and whether June-quarter revenue benefits from the delayed base-model launch .

BofA is not making a bearish call on Apple.

It is warning that Wall Street may be looking at the right business through the wrong quarterly lens.
